title: Adversarial assess loop: closeout Step 5.5 + recursive fresh-eyes + out-of-scope bead-filing
description:
Child of polyglot-pdf-7dkb (SPEAR adoption epic).

.claude/agents/fresh-eyes-reviewer.md, two changes:
1. ADVERSARIAL framing: "Find every place the produced changes do NOT meet the
   required rubric criteria; your job is complete only when you cannot find any
   remaining gap." Gap-exhaustion, not approval -- the assessor "wins" by
   finding gaps. Approval-seeking is the failure mode.
2. Out-of-scope bug filing: genuine bugs outside the current bead's exit
   criteria get filed as NEW beads directly by fresh-eyes (Bash is in its tool
   list; pull/push-bracketed bd create, body includes >= 1 exit criterion +
   surfaces metadata), NOT escalated to the executor. Findings output lists
   filed bead IDs.

.claude/skills/closeout/SKILL.md:
- New Step 5.5 (pre-PR Assess): orchestrator scores each exit criterion
  PASS/FAIL with one-line evidence; any FAIL -> fix before opening the PR;
  missing criteria -> write retrospective rubric, score, note gaps. Scorecard
  goes in the PR body under an "Exit criteria" section.
- Step 6 amendment: recursive fresh-eyes loop as the INNER assess cycle:
  execute -> fresh-eyes (adversarial, criteria passed in) -> fix gaps ->
  fresh-eyes again -> ... until "no gap found" (MAX_FRESH_EYES_ROUNDS = 3),
  THEN open the PR. Codex (when credits available) is the outer review; when
  unavailable, the last fresh-eyes gap-free verdict is the review record, noted
  in the PR body. Subagent TIMEOUT/ERROR surfaces to orchestrator, never
  silently skipped.

docs/doctrine/review-flow.md: document the assess layer (scorecard in PR body,
fresh-eyes rubric verdict, the no-Codex fallback).

## Exit criteria (inherits epic criterion 3)

- /closeout SKILL.md contains Step 5.5 and the recursive adversarial fresh-eyes
  loop; fresh-eyes-reviewer.md carries the adversarial framing and the
  bead-filing protocol; the implementing PR's body carries the criteria
  scorecard (self-demonstrating).

title: Exit-criteria convention (creation-time norm) + /next-bead claim-time gate
description:

title: EPIC: SPEAR partial adoption -- epic-level planning, exit criteria, adversarial assess loop
description:
## Why (L1, maintainer)

Move the software factory toward greater autonomy: tight scoping to prevent
drift, accountability to predetermined measurable success criteria,
self-correction via multi-agent cross-checking (no one agent does all of plan +
execute + assess), and token-efficient model tiering (expensive models at
decision gates only -- never bug-hunting or grepping).

## How (L2, collaborative -- settled in planning session 2026-06-10/11)

SPEAR (Scope, Plan, Execute, Assess, Resolve) adopted as a PER-FEATURE (epic)
process, not per-bead. Scope+Plan happen at epic-planning time via a new
/plan-epic skill (orchestrator-owned; subagents cannot converse with the
maintainer). Beads become MECE epic children inheriting exit criteria, or
standalone tickets with 1-3 criteria written at CREATION time (claim-time gate
as backstop for the legacy backlog). The assess loop is recursive ADVERSARIAL
fresh-eyes ("find every gap" framing, not "approve"), looped until no gap is
found; fresh-eyes also files out-of-scope bugs as new beads directly.

Full plan: docs/sprint_2_spear-adoption_plan.md (this PR). Research:
docs/journal/entries/2026-06-10-bd-1crj-spear-workflow-proposal.md (PR #151).

## Exit criteria (epic rubric -- scored at closeout)

1. /plan-epic skill exists; a dry read-through yields the rubric format, MECE
   checklist, criteria-inheritance rule, and maintainer approval gate without
   referencing missing docs.
2. workflow.md documents the exit-criteria convention (creation-time norm,
   claim-time backstop); /next-bead contains the claim-time gate.
3. /closeout contains the pre-PR Assess step and the recursive adversarial
   fresh-eyes loop; the implementing PR's own body carries the criteria
   scorecard (self-demonstrating).
4. CLAUDE.md and docs/INDEX.md point at docs/doctrine/planning.md;
   scripts/check_doc_freshness.py passes.

title: Gemini goes silent on field 2 (no tool call, no audio) while overlay still mounted -- the real demo hang
description:
REMOTE DEMO repro (2026-06-10, polyglot-demo-aa709, backend session web_gDG8eflVfns). The field-2 hang: after confirm_field on field 1, the client stopped streaming mic audio to the backend (backend got 0 inbound frames for ~4 min, then idle-timed-out + reconnected at 18:01). NOT caused by the resize/mic bug nlfc (that came later; maintainer correction).

=== INVESTIGATION (session ending, context full) ===

RULED OUT -- hypothesis (a) native-VAD send stuck MUTED: the demo console showed 'Setting push-to-talk mode: false' + 'Unmuting input - audio processing active', so pttModeEnabled=false and inputMuted=false. Under native VAD, shouldSendAudioChunk (frontend/src/shared/audioManager.ts L58-76) returns TRUE in that state (nativeVadEnabled && !(ptt && muted) -> true). So gate 1 (the mode/mute gate) was PASSING. The mic worklet was producing chunks and they cleared shouldSendAudioChunk.

LEADING HYPOTHESIS -- gate 2, the connection-status send gate: the audio-send callback in frontend/src/shared/connection.ts (startRecording, ~L658-663) is:
    await audioManager.startRecording((audioData) => {
      if (connection && connection.getStatus() === 'connected') {
        connection.sendAudio(audioData)
      }
    })
This SILENTLY DROPS every mic chunk whenever WebFormConnection.status !== exactly 'connected' (e.g. 'switching_section', 'reconnecting', 'connecting', 'idle_timeout'). The chunk is gathered by the worklet, passes shouldSendAudioChunk, reaches this callback, and is discarded with NO log and NO recovery. This exactly matches the symptom: backend saw ZERO inbound frames while the FRONTEND believed it was connected and kept RECEIVING Gemini audio (incoming audio is NOT status-gated, so chunks #600/#700 kept arriving). connection.getStatus() maps to WebFormConnection.status (connection.ts L555-556).

OPEN QUESTION (needs a live repro or the FULL frontend console -- the maintainer's paste was partial): WHICH transition left WebFormConnection.status != 'connected' after the field-1 confirm. Field 1 -> field 2 is a SAME-SECTION advance (both in 'Part 1.1', field_count=9, JIT Mode=False per backend log), so handleConfirmFieldRequest's computeNextField should return field 2 and SKIP the section-switch block (webFormConnection.ts ~L1207 'if (!nextField)'), leaving status 'connected'. YET the backend did a full session RESTART at 18:01 (web_KFMMK0Nboys, 'Next field to fill is #2'), which is a switch/reconnect -- so SOMETHING did treat the advance as a switch/restart, OR the status was already stranded from the earlier post-disclaimer first-section switch. status->'connected' is set at webFormConnection.ts L482 (handleSessionReady), L1027 (handleSectionSwitched), L2286; status leaves 'connected' at L925/L2046/L2173 (switching_section), L1607 (reconnecting), L435/L1590 (idle_timeout), L1527 (error). Need to find which fired between 17:56:54 (confirm) and the user's field-2 attempts.

STATUS-GATE TRANSITIONS TO CHASE NEXT:
- Did the post-disclaimer first-section switch (startSection/switchToSection) ever land status back at 'connected' via session_ready/section_switched? Field 1 DID fill+confirm (17:56), which REQUIRES audio reaching the backend, so status WAS 'connected' during field 1. So the stranding happened AT/AFTER the field-1 confirm, not before.
- Does the next_field_hint send after a same-section confirm, or the confirm round-trip itself (wpw.2 sync confirm), transition status?
- Is there a watchdog/recovery path (VoiceOverlay activity watchdog) that flips status on silence?

RECOMMENDED FIX (independent of which transition strands the status -- this is a latent bug regardless): the audio-send callback must NOT silently drop the user's voice on a non-'connected' status. At minimum LOG it loudly (rate-limited) so a dropped-audio window is visible in console + (if reachable) surfaced; better, BUFFER-or-flush on reconnect, or widen the gate to also send during 'switching_section' if the socket is OPEN, or re-arm the send path when status returns to 'connected'. A gate that discards mic audio with zero observability is exactly why this was invisible for ~4 min until the idle-timeout. Decide buffer-vs-widen-gate after confirming the stranding transition (a buffer risks sending stale audio to the wrong/new session; widening the gate risks sending to a half-open socket -- so pair either with a session-id/epoch check).

DECISIVE NEXT STEP: live repro via the voice-harness (.claude/skills/voice-harness, GEMINI_API_KEY is available in env) driving field-1 -> confirm -> field-2, logging connection.getStatus() and whether sendAudio is reached at each captured chunk; OR ship the harden-the-gate-with-logging fix to the demo and have the maintainer reproduce once with the new logs. Maintainer dismissed the approach-choice; left for the next session to decide.

RELATED: cwsy (the ~49s field-1 round-trip latency -- SAME session-restart machinery, likely same root area), nlfc (the resize/mic-kill bug -- real but a separate red herring for THIS hang). No code was changed for irck this session; this is investigation only. PR #145 (wpw.3) is MERGED and unrelated to this.
close_reason: Investigation complete (no code change). Root cause narrowed: native-VAD mute RULED OUT; leading cause is the connection-status audio-send gate (connection.ts ~L660) silently dropping mic chunks when WebFormConnection.status != 'connected'. Full analysis + recommended fix (harden the gate so audio is never silently dropped + observability; pair any buffer/widen with a session-epoch check) + decisive next step (voice-harness live repro) recorded in the bead. Closing per maintainer (session retiring); a follow-up implementation bead should be filed when the fix is picked up. Related: cwsy (same session-restart machinery), nlfc (separate resize bug).

title: Resize-flip (desktop<->mobile overlay swap) mid-session kills the mic -- Gemini hangs, field never fills
description: REAL BUG, but NOT the cause of the 2026-06-10 field-2 hang (maintainer correction). The resize-flip mic-kill is genuine: resizing the browser across the 768px breakpoint mid-session swaps VoiceOverlay <-> VoiceOverlayMobile; the new overlay mounts onto the live shared ConnectionManager via its alreadyLive early-return (VoiceOverlayMobile.tsx ~L121-137; same guard VoiceOverlay.tsx ~L137-150, bd 6vo) which SKIPS handleConnect() -- and startRecording() only runs inside handleConnect() (VoiceOverlayMobile.tsx ~L762 / VoiceOverlay.tsx ~L604). So mic capture is never re-armed after the old overlay's audio teardown ('Stream not initialized'/'Source node not initialized' from Z.destroy). The WS/session SURVIVES (shared manager not disconnected on unmount, VoiceOverlay.tsx L494). FIX: on the alreadyLive remount, re-arm mic capture (startRecording + re-sync PTT/native-VAD audio) without reconnecting/re-disclaiming; add a regression test driving a live-session desktop<->mobile flip asserting startRecording on the shared manager. CAVEAT (maintainer, 2026-06-10): in the observed demo session the resize happened AFTER Gemini had ALREADY gone silent -- the user waited + voice-prompted 2-3x first, THEN opened the dev console which squished the viewport past the breakpoint. So this bug did NOT cause that hang; the field-2 silence is a SEPARATE upstream issue (see polyglot-pdf-cwsy / a new bead) that occurred while the DESKTOP overlay was still mounted. Priority stays P1 (demo-blocking on any real resize) but it is decoupled from the field-2-silence investigation.

title: WS-B core: cooperative receive-loop shutdown (y4a ordering + switch lock + shutdown-flag lock)
description:
KEYSTONE demo fix (re-scoped per finalized plan 2026-06-09, plan file please-check-out-the-serene-church.md). Replace cancel-from-within with a cooperative loop exit so the switch_section FunctionResponse is delivered on the OLD session BEFORE teardown ("respond, cooperatively drain, swap off-task").

ADAPTER (live_ai_gemini.py): new state _close_after_flush + _closed_event; sync begin_graceful_shutdown() (no awaits/locks; sets _close_after_flush + _intentional_shutdown, clears _session_ready; returns the event); set_callbacks resets the flag + fresh event when spawning the new _bg_task (a stale flag must never kill the next session); _run_session_loop wrapped in try/finally setting _closed_event (anti-hang guarantee); receive loop breaks after send_tool_response (~L1600) AND at the loop-continue point (~L1767) when flagged (single flush point for BOTH tool-call paths); finalize() unchanged for outside callers + top guard (if called from _bg_task itself: log error + begin_graceful_shutdown + return -- self-cancel can never be reintroduced); move shutdown-flag mutations (L627-631) inside _task_lock (the shutdown-race fix).

SERVICE (form_filling_service.py): _switch_lock + _switch_task strong ref; handle_switch_section keeps the request_section_info round-trip inline, guards on an in-progress switch (return success:false), calls begin_graceful_shutdown(), spawns _complete_section_switch(closed, info) via create_task, and RETURNS the success payload (= the FunctionResponse delivered on the old session); _complete_section_switch awaits closed (wait_for 5s; the finalize() inside switch_to_section hard-cancels as backstop) then awaits switch_to_section (body unchanged), with a catch-all except that logs + notifies the FE (a detached task must never swallow); switch_to_section body wrapped in _switch_lock -- serializes AI-initiated vs manual switches (ABSORBED FROM WS-D, plan hazard 1). finalize idempotency / once-only cost summary verified here (moved from WS-D).

TESTS red-first (test_section_switching.py): fake LiveAI session recording call ORDER -- switch_section response-send strictly BEFORE session close/cancel (replaces the .called-only asserts that hide this today); swap-task-awaits-closure unit (start_session never runs before _closed_event is set -- prevents two live loops sharing callbacks, plan hazard 5); two concurrent switch_to_section -> one consistent session + one cost summary; shutdown-flags-under-lock unit. Must not regress uov.10. Gate: the 8k8 multi-section scenario flips green/stable.

title: [epic] Harden the core voice round-trip loop (demo-first)
description:
Make the core voice loop (Gemini speaks -> user answers -> audio up -> tool call -> frontend round-trip -> FunctionResponse -> advance) demonstrably carry a multi-field, multi-section voice session without resets, stalls, silent failures, or false confirmations -- for a possible VC demo. Demo-readiness is priority 1; TEXT-token-cost reduction is priority 2.

title: fix(harness): undeclared surfaces should NOT collide with everything -- only positively-stated overlaps block
description:
The R1 write-overlap guard (scripts/bd_safe.py _surfaces_overlap) treats an empty/UNKNOWN surface set as 'collides with everything' (fail-closed). In practice the common case is just a bead nobody annotated (e.g. polyglot-pdf-akn, a backend-only bug with no declared surfaces), which then BLOCKS the entire next-bead board -- every other ready bead reports 'overlaps akn'. This froze uov.4 (a frontend-only test bead) behind akn (a backend-only fix) with provably-disjoint footprints.

Maintainer decision (2026-06-09): the guard should only block on POSITIVELY-STATED, actually-overlapping surfaces. An empty surface set on EITHER side -- whether unannotated or from a tooling failure -- means 'no stated surface to collide on' and must NOT block. It would be the rare bead that legitimately blocks everything; the default should be permissive, not conservative.

Fix: _surfaces_overlap returns False when either side is empty (was True). Update the unit tests (test_surfaces_overlap_unknown_policy and the next_bead/claim integration tests that assert the old collide-all behavior) and the doctrine note (docs/doctrine/workflow.md) to match. Reverses the conservative half of bd polyglot-pdf-8y7 (the PR-derivation half stays useful but is no longer load-bearing for correctness).

title: fix(voice): FormFillingService missing send_activity_end -- crashed WS on every PTT turn
description:
Root cause of 'connection resets every time I talk to Gemini' (reported on dev deploy 2026-06-09).

The /ws/fill route handler calls service.send_activity_end() on every vad_activity_end message (sent after the disclaimer accept AND after every push-to-talk release). FormFillingService had send_activity_start (delegating to AudioHandler) but NO send_activity_end -- so the call raised AttributeError, propagated out of the receive loop, crashed the ASGI handler, and closed the WebSocket. Frontend auto-reconnected; next PTT release crashed it again => reset-on-every-turn loop.

AudioHandler.send_activity_end and LiveAI.send_activity_end already existed; only the service-level passthrough was missing (regression from the native-VAD/PTT confirm-flow work around PR #126).

Fix: add the 4-line delegation mirroring send_activity_start (backend/services/form_filling_service.py).

VERIFIED end-to-end on the local stack + real Gemini via the voice-harness: multiple vad_activity_end round-trips now flow cleanly (zero AttributeError / Exception in ASGI), session stays alive across turns, and the full update_form_fields round-trip completes (field p1_line1_aliennumber filled '1234567', tool_response success=true). Backend log evidence: 'Received vad_activity_end -> Sending activity_end to Gemini' at 11:05:30/11:05:47/11:06:08 with no crash.

Note: confirm_field tool-call reliability (ssConfirmed) is a SEPARATE model-behavior issue (bd gemini-3p1-skips-update-form-fields / polyglot-pdf-0ux), not this connection bug.

title: INVESTIGATION: audit the full tool-call round-trip (Gemini speaks -> user -> tool call -> validate -> tool_response -> Gemini speaks)
description:
Trace and audit the complete conversational round-trip for tool calls, end to end, looking for where it can silently break or desync. The maintainer suspects something is going wrong in this flow.

THE FLOW (as the maintainer framed it):
1. Gemini speaks to the user.
2. User responds (audio).
3. Gemini triggers a tool call (update_form_fields / confirm_field / get_field_value / get_form_status / switch_section).
4. The system validates the tool call and produces a tool response.
5. Gemini receives the tool_response and speaks to the user again.

KEY GROUNDED FILE PATHS (verified 2026-06-08):
- backend/adapters/live_ai_gemini.py: receives tool calls via TWO parallel paths -- the model_turn.parts function_call path (~L1306-1425) AND the event.tool_call path (~L1432-1527). Each builds its own types.FunctionResponse and they share the 'responses' list flushed via session.send_tool_response (~L1553). The two paths differ: parts-path FunctionResponse includes id=call_id (L1421); event.tool_call-path OMITS id (comment L1520 'should NOT include id'). Divergence worth auditing.
- backend/services/callback_handler.py: on_tool_call dispatch (L167-245) -> _handle_update_form_fields_tool (L247-325), _handle_confirm_field_tool (L399), get_form_status/get_field_value/switch_section. update_form_fields VALIDATION IS BACKEND-SIDE (self._handle_update_fields), not frontend; frontend only receives a 'form_updated' push (L101) and applies it.
- backend/services/form_filling_service.py: wires set_callbacks (L167/430).
- frontend/src/webFormConnection.ts: handleFormUpdate (~L440, the update path that marks fields UNCONFIRMED + sends dependency_error back over WS at L485) and handleFormUpdated (~L502, applies backend 'form_updated' push). onFieldUpdate callback at L497/588.
- frontend/src/shared/connection.ts: onFieldUpdate (L280) applies accepted updates to DOM; metrics.recordToolCall can REJECT updates as hallucinations (L298-308) -- a frontend-side drop that the backend/Gemini tool_response does NOT know about (possible desync source).

SUSPECTED PROBLEM AREAS TO VERIFY (not yet confirmed bugs):
- Mental-model gap: maintainer expects the FRONTEND to validate the tool call; actually the BACKEND validates and the frontend's only 'validation' is the hallucination-reject in connection.ts (L300) + dependency lock check in webFormConnection.ts (L450). Confirm which is authoritative and whether they can disagree.
- Two tool-call receive paths in the adapter with divergent FunctionResponse construction (id vs no-id). Determine which path actually fires for native-audio models and whether the other is dead/duplicate.
- Frontend hallucination-reject (connection.ts L300) silently drops an update AFTER the backend already told Gemini the field was applied -> Gemini believes a value is saved that the DOM never shows.
- response_payload defaulting to {} when a callback returns None (adapter L1415/1516) -- does Gemini get a meaningful 'saved/failed' signal, or an empty ack it can misread as success?
- Related closed beads for context: polyglot-pdf-5oq (3.1 skips update_form_fields), polyglot-pdf-kbf (full Gemini I/O dev logging + A/B toggle -- USE THIS LOGGING to capture a real round-trip), gemini-3p1-skips-update-form-fields memory.

DELIVERABLE: a written trace of the real flow (with the dev-logging from kbf if a live session is run), a list of confirmed desync/break points, and either fixes (small) or follow-up beads (larger). Start by reading docs/components/voice-ai.md and docs/components/websocket-routing.md.

comments.author: caellwynai-josh
comments.text:
STATIC TRACE COMPLETE (no live session yet). Confirmed the round-trip and found TWO real desync points + one latent inconsistency.

== THE REAL FLOW (verified against code) ==
1. Gemini speaks (audio out via on_audio).
2. User speaks; audio streamed over WS to backend -> Gemini.
3. Gemini emits a tool call. Adapter receives it on ONE of two paths (live_ai_gemini.py): model_turn.parts[].function_call (PRIMARY for native-audio models) OR event.tool_call (alternate). Both -> CallbackHandler.on_tool_call.
4. VALIDATION IS BACKEND-SIDE (callback_handler._handle_update_form_fields_tool): normalize -> _handle_update_fields (validate+apply to backend form_state) -> send_form_update() pushes a 'form_updated' WS msg to the frontend -> returns a tool_response with applied_fields/validation_errors/unknown_fields.
5. Adapter sends tool_response via session.send_tool_response. Gemini reads it back and speaks.
   NOTE: this corrects the maintainer's mental model -- the FRONTEND does NOT validate update_form_fields; the backend does. The frontend only (a) applies the pushed form_updated, (b) can reject as hallucination, (c) checks dependency-locks in webFormConnection.handleFormUpdate.

== CONFIRMED DESYNC #1: confirm_field 2s-timeout reads as 'form done' ==
request_coordinator.request_next_field_hint() (L135) wait_for(timeout=2.0); on TimeoutError returns None. _handle_confirm_field_tool (callback_handler L439) then returns message 'Field confirmed. All fields confirmed.' -- IDENTICAL to genuine completion. A slow frontend hint round-trip (>2s) makes Gemini believe the whole form is finished and wrap up. The tool_response has no 'timed out vs truly done' distinction. Doc tool-call-flow.md L78-81 already flags this as a hypothesis; code confirms it.

== CONFIRMED DESYNC #2: frontend hallucination-reject silently drops an already-acked update ==
connection.ts onFieldUpdate (L295-320) calls metrics.recordToolCall; if within BARGE_IN_GRACE_PERIOD_MS of a barge-in, returns 'reject' (metrics.ts L209-220) and the update is NOT applied to the DOM. But the BACKEND already validated+applied it to its form_state AND already returned applied_fields to Gemini (step 4-5). Result: Gemini believes the value is saved and reads it back; the DOM never shows it; nothing re-syncs (metrics.ts L220 just returns, no WS message back). Field silently lost while Gemini asserts success.

== LATENT INCONSISTENCY #3 (low pri): divergent FunctionResponse construction ==
parts-path builds types.FunctionResponse WITH id=call_id (L1421); event.tool_call-path builds it WITHOUT id (L1520, comment 'should NOT include id'). Only matters if both paths fire for the same model; for native-audio the parts path is primary. Worth reconciling but not a live bug unless an A/B model uses the alternate path.

NEXT: capture a real session with the kbf dev-logging (USE_PREMIUM_MODEL A/B, backend/logs/gemini_<date>.jsonl) to see which desync actually bites in practice, then fix #1 (cheap: distinguish timeout from done in the tool_response) and decide on #2 (either suppress the backend ack until frontend confirms, or have the frontend re-notify backend on reject).

comments.author: caellwynai-josh
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION: why a tool_response can fail to reach Gemini (she blocks waiting for it). Traced every tool's response path. Backend handlers are robust; the gaps are in the ADAPTER and in switch_section's self-teardown.

== SAFE PATHS (verified -- these always produce a response, even on frontend timeout) ==
- get_form_status: request_form_state() returns {} on 5s timeout -> 'No fields filled' response. OK.
- get_field_value: request_field_value() degrades -> {found:False,...}. OK.
- switch_section HANDLER (handle_switch_section): request_section_info() None/timeout -> {success:False,'... timed out'}. OK *as a value* -- but see BLOCKER #3, the response never gets SENT.
- confirm_field: fixed earlier (HINT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT sentinel).
- unknown tool: returns {} (non-blocking). session_id is None: returns None -> adapter coerces to {} and still sends. OK.

== BLOCKER #1 (adapter, parts-path): FunctionResponse dropped when call_id is missing ==
live_ai_gemini.py L1418:  gates the responses.append on the model_turn.parts path. call_id = getattr(function_call,'id',None) (L1309). If Gemini emits a function_call on the parts path with NO id (or empty id), call_id is falsy -> NO FunctionResponse appended -> send_tool_response never called for that call -> Gemini blocks forever. The alternate event.tool_call path (L1519) gates only on  and does NOT require id, so the two paths disagree on exactly the failure that blocks. Fix: gate on tool_name only (id is optional; SDK matches by order) OR always append. LOW-ish freq but a hard hang when it hits.

== BLOCKER #2 (adapter, parts-path): callback EXCEPTION still drops the response when call_id missing ==
Same path: on a callback exception (L1394) response_payload stays None -> coerced to {} (L1416) -> but append still gated on call_id (L1418). event.tool_call path is resilient here (L1515 coerces, L1519 appends on tool_name alone). So a raising callback on the parts-path + missing id = no response = block. Fix folds into #1 (append on tool_name; never let an exception skip the append).

== BLOCKER #3 (THE BIG ONE -- switch_section tears down the task that must send its own response) ==
Sequence: Gemini -> switch_section -> on_tool_call -> _handle_switch_section_tool -> handle_switch_section -> AWAITS switch_to_section() INLINE (form_filling_service L847) -> switch_to_section calls self._live_ai.finalize() (L580) -> finalize() does self._bg_task.cancel() (live_ai_gemini L603). The bg task IS the  loop (L1108) that is CURRENTLY RUNNING this very callback. So the receive loop cancels ITSELF from inside its own tool callback. When the callback returns, the downstream code that appends the FunctionResponse (L1418-1425) and calls session.send_tool_response (L1553) is on the SAME cancelled task and on the OLD session that finalize() just closed -- it never runs / sends to a dead session. The switch_section tool call gets NO response on the session that issued it.
Why it often 'works' anyway: switch_to_section -> start_session opens a NEW session that re-sends system instruction + initial_field_hint and re-greets (L1082 'Waiting for user to speak'), so Gemini proceeds driven by the NEW session, not by a response to her switch_section call. It HANGS when that new-session turn-start does NOT fire cleanly: token re-fetch fails, no greeting/turn injected, or native-VAD waits on user audio that never comes -> Gemini sits with an unanswered switch_section call and silence. This matches the 'she gets stuck in a blocking way' report most directly.
Fix options (design call -- not an obvious one-liner): (a) send the switch_section FunctionResponse on the OLD session BEFORE finalize() (defer the section teardown until after the adapter has flushed the response), or (b) make switch_section non-blocking: return the tool response immediately, then perform the session swap asynchronously, or (c) have the adapter special-case switch_section: append+send_tool_response, THEN allow the swap. (a) is the most faithful to the Live API contract.

NEXT: capture one real switch_section round-trip with kbf dev-logging to confirm the orphaned-response timing (look for a tool_call path='model_turn.parts' or 'event.tool_call' for switch_section with NO following tool_response on that session id, then a session_open for the next section). Then fix #1/#2 together (cheap, clearly-correct) and decide #3's approach.

comments.author: caellwynai-josh
comments.text:
FIXED #1 + #2 (adapter model_turn.parts path dropping the FunctionResponse -> Gemini blocks on the first tool-call/response loop).

Root cause: on the model_turn.parts receive path, the response append was gated on 'tool_name AND call_id'. A function_call arriving with no 'id' produced NO FunctionResponse (#1); and although a callback exception was caught and response_payload coerced to {}, the same call_id gate could still skip the append (#2). Either way send_tool_response was never called for that call and Gemini waited forever. The sibling event.tool_call path was already resilient (gates on tool_name alone, omits id).

Fix (live_ai_gemini.py): append on tool_name only; build FunctionResponse with id ONLY when present (SDK matches by order otherwise). This makes the parts path match the event.tool_call path and guarantees every named call -- including one whose callback raised -- gets at least an empty {} ack.

Tests: added test_model_turn_parts_tool_call_without_id_still_responds and test_model_turn_parts_tool_call_exception_still_responds (backend/tests/unit/test_live_ai_gemini.py). title: PTT as a client-side audio gate layered on always-on native VAD (toggle was dead in native mode)
description:
BLOCKING demo bug. Symptoms: (1) the Input-Mode toggle does nothing when clicked, (2) the PTT/Hold-to-Talk button is missing, (3) Gemini does not hear the user at all.

Root cause: the default backend mode is native Gemini VAD (DISABLE_GEMINI_VAD=false). The tlc/333/#110 work made native VAD and PTT MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE -- in native mode the PTT button is hidden (pushToTalkMode && isConnected && !nativeVad), the toggle is disabled (disabled={nativeVad}), and handlePushToTalkToggle early-returns on isNativeVad(). Worse, the toggle's handler guard checks connectionManager.isNativeVad() (a closure var set once from the handshake and NEVER reset) while the disabled/label use the React nativeVad state (gated on status==connected), so when disconnected/idle the toggle renders ENABLED but the handler early-returns -> looks active, does nothing. And audioManager's native-VAD path streamed ALL audio bypassing inputMuted, so even a working PTT mute could not gate audio in native mode.

Fix (per maintainer direction): keep native VAD ALWAYS on at the backend, but make PTT a CLIENT-SIDE AUDIO GATE layered on top (useful in noisy rooms so background noise does not trip Gemini's VAD). Decoupled PTT's audio gating from native VAD while KEEPING native VAD's suppression of manual activity signals (Silero activity_start/end stay suppressed -- Gemini owns turn detection; PTT only decides which client bytes are sent).

Changes (frontend-only, no wire/backend change):
- audioManager.ts: extracted shouldSendAudioChunk() pure gate; native mode now honors inputMuted when PTT is on (PTT off = continuous). setPTTMode keeps the worklet RMS gate bypassed under native VAD regardless of PTT.
- VoiceOverlay.tsx + VoiceOverlayMobile.tsx: removed the isNativeVad() early-returns in the toggle handler + PTT-sync; PTT button and toggle now always available; relabeled PTT/Auto (no more dead Native/disabled).
- New audioGate.test.ts (5 cases) covers the three-way routing incl. native+PTT+muted -> withhold.

Verify on the live stack: native VAD still works (PTT off = continuous, Gemini hears continuously); PTT on = press to talk gates audio; toggle flips live.

title: BUG: I-90 read-only unlock never fires (filler reads conditional_behavior, gold puts flag-change under conditional_logic)
description:
BUG (production filler). Read-only-field unlock NEVER fires for I-90 -- found during 7a9.14 review (fresh-eyes + Copilot both flagged it). The I-90 gold schema stores the unlock instruction under conditional_logic.pdf_field_flag_change, but the production filler reads it from conditional_behavior.pdf_field_flag_change. The two keys never line up, so no read-only field is ever unlocked before filling.

EVIDENCE:
- backend/routes/pdf_fill_routes.py apply_field_flag_changes (line ~176-186) does: conditional_behavior = field_obj.get("conditional_behavior"); pdf_field_flag_change = conditional_behavior.get("pdf_field_flag_change"). It is called (lines ~266-267, ~311-312, ~404-405) with field_obj.get("conditional_behavior").
- form-kits/i-90/schema.json: 16 fields carry the unlock, and ALL of them put pdf_field_flag_change under conditional_logic; their conditional_behavior holds ONLY {"unlock_method":"flip_readonly_bit"} (no pdf_field_flag_change). Affected fields include p1_line5a/5b/5c_*name (previous name, shown when name changed), p1_line6c/7b_aptsteflrnumber, p2_line2h1_cityandstate, p2_checkbox2[5], p2_checkbox3, p4_line1a/1b/1c_accomodationrequested, p5_line1b_language, p5_line2_nameofrepresentative, p6/p7_line3b_aptsteflrnumber, p7_checkbox7extend.

IMPACT: every conditionally-unlocked read-only field on I-90 silently fails to fill in the live app -- e.g. a user who changed their name cannot fill previous-name; apartment/suite/floor numbers, accommodation text, interpreter language, etc. all stay locked.

FIX OPTIONS (decide):
1. Make the filler read pdf_field_flag_change from conditional_logic (where the gold puts it) -- one-line change in apply_field_flag_changes + its call sites; lowest-risk, matches existing data.
2. OR move pdf_field_flag_change to conditional_behavior in the gold schema(s) and keep the filler as-is -- but then every schema/extractor must emit it there.
Option 1 is recommended (data already exists in conditional_logic across the gold). Whichever is chosen, the 7a9.14 schema_contract.py choice-field rule + the round-trip harness should assert the unlock actually fires (the harness applies the flag-flip from conditional_behavior today, mirroring the buggy production path; update both together once the key is decided).

RELATION: surfaced by the 7a9.14 round-trip harness work; documented in docs/research/2026-06-07-7a9.14-checkbox-radio-roundtrip-findings.md. Sibling to bd polyglot-pdf-7a9.15 (the other live I-90 fill bug, p3_race).
close_reason: Read-only unlock fixed (read pdf_field_flag_change from conditional_logic first). Shipped in PR #117. Codex review CLEAN (thumbs-up); fresh-eyes CLEAN. Route-level regression test added; full suite 219 passed.

title: BUG: I-90 p3_race checkbox group won't round-trip fill (missing [0] + semantic values)
description:
BUG (production schema). The I-90 gold schema (form-kits/i-90/schema.json) field p3_race (the Race "select all that apply" checkbox group, Part 3) would NOT round-trip fill -- discovered by the 7a9.14 round-trip harness (scripts/bakeoff/roundtrip_fill.py). Two defects, both isolated to this one field; every other I-90 choice field round-trips 100%:

1. WIDGET NAMES MISSING THE [0] INDEX. The 5 options carry pdf_field_name "P3_checkbox7_White" / "_Asian" / "_Black" / "_Indian" / "_Hawaiian", but the actual PDF widgets are "form1[0].#subform[2].P3_checkbox7_White[0]" etc (with a trailing [0]). The production filler's find_widget (backend/routes/pdf_fill_routes.py) matches exact-then-endswith; "...White[0]".endswith("P3_checkbox7_White") is FALSE, so none of the 5 race widgets are found and the field silently does not fill. Fix: append "[0]" to each of the 5 option.pdf_field_name (verified: adding [0] makes all 5 match).

2. SEMANTIC option.value INSTEAD OF THE WIDGET-LEAF CONVENTION. p3_race options use value "white"/"asian"/"black"/"native_american"/"pacific_islander", whereas every other I-90 choice field uses the widget-leaf identifier as option.value (e.g. "P1_checkbox4[0]"). The filler selects the widget by matching the app-sent value against option.value, so the value convention must be consistent for selection to work end-to-end (see bd 7a9.14 #1). Decide: either bring p3_race onto the widget-leaf convention (value="P3_checkbox7_White[0]" ...) like the rest of I-90, OR confirm the frontend/voice layer sends the semantic values for this field specifically -- but the inconsistency is a latent bug.

EVIDENCE: roundtrip_fill.py on form-kits/i-90/schema.json scores choice_fill_success 23/28; the 5 misses are exactly these p3_race options (all "widget_not_found"). Excluding p3_race the gold scores 23/23 choice + 108/108 text = 100%.

SCOPE: this is the LIVE i-90 form schema the app fills, not a research artifact -- a real user filling Race today gets nothing written. Fix the 5 pdf_field_names (defect 1) at minimum; resolve the value convention (defect 2) per the 7a9.14 convention. Keep the existing working shape of every other field intact.
close_reason: p3_race fill fixed (brought onto I-90 widget-leaf convention: full-path pdf_field_name + leaf value with [0]). Shipped in PR #117. Codex review CLEAN (thumbs-up); fresh-eyes CLEAN. Round-trip harness now 28/28 choice fill on I-90 gold; route-level regression test added.

title: Stop Gemini speaking the raw field_id aloud (legacy system instruction)
description:
## Context
Live test 2026-06-07 (session fss_mq4c81vs): Gemini reads the raw field_id aloud. Root cause: frontend formatNextFieldHint (frontend/src/navigation.ts:343) builds 'Next field to fill is #1: <spoken name> (field_id: <id>, type: <type>)' -- the field_id is in the SPOKEN hint. That hint flows: webFormConnection.ts:700 -> WS (change_spoken_language / next_field_hint) -> backend send_initiating_message -> INITIATING_MESSAGE template (config.py:383) -> Gemini speaks it verbatim. The JIT_SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION already says 'Never read field IDs aloud (use spoken names only)' but the LEGACY SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION (the one in use) does NOT. Fix: add that constraint to SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION AND stop the field_id reaching the spoken path (strip '(field_id:...)' in send_initiating_message before formatting, the no-wire-change option). Gemini still needs the field_id for the tool call -- it's in the FIELDS/fields_json block of the system instruction, so stripping it from the spoken hint is safe.
acceptance_criteria: Gemini no longer reads the field_id (e.g. 'p1_line1_aliennumber') aloud when asking for a field. Two parts: (1) the spoken hint sent via INITIATING_MESSAGE no longer embeds '(field_id: ..., type: ...)' OR the backend strips it before speaking; (2) the legacy SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION gains the 'Never read field IDs aloud (use spoken names only)' constraint the JIT_SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION already has. Verify the field_id is still available to Gemini for the update_form_fields tool call (don't break filling). Probe/inspect the initiating message no longer contains a spoken field_id.

title: Fix 3.1 skipping update_form_fields: force tool call before verbal confirm (prompt)
description:
## Context
Root cause CONFIRMED via backend/scripts/probe_tool_call.py (bd polyglot-pdf-kbf debug session, 2026-06-07): with the real SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION + TOOL_DECLARATIONS, 3.1 jumps to step-3 verbal confirmation ('Your A-Number is X, is that correct?' / 'I have entered X') WITHOUT first emitting the step-2 update_form_fields tool call -- 0/3 runs. 2.5 calls it correctly 2/2. So nothing reaches the backend, the field never saves, and she says 'trouble saving'. It is a 3.1 workflow-following regression (not validation/tooling/websocket -- all ruled out; probe bypasses front+back end). Fix: harden the WORKFLOW section of SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION so 3.1 MUST call update_form_fields and see success BEFORE speaking any confirmation. 3.1 is a thinking model (emits a 'thought' part) so it may be reasoning-about-confirming instead of acting. Iterate the prompt against the probe (multiple runs per change) until 3.1 is reliable; keep 3.1 (reliable audio) rather than falling back to 2.5 (intermittent-silent, bd daa).
acceptance_criteria: probe_tool_call.py shows gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview emits update_form_fields with correct args BEFORE any verbal read-back, reliably across multiple runs (target: at least 5/5), using the production SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION. 2.5 still works (no regression). The fix is in the system instruction (backend/config.py), verified via the probe before any live test.
notes: SCOPE REVISED (probe finding): prompt-only CANNOT fix 3.1 within the same-turn talk+confirm workflow. 3.1 calls the tool reliably ONLY when the prompt mentions no speech (4/5); ANY confirm/acknowledge/next-field speech instruction drops it to 0/5 and triggers confabulated 'trouble saving'. Maintainer decision (2026-06-07): RESTRUCTURE -- the fill turn emits ONLY the tool call (no speech), confirmation moves to a SEPARATE turn / UI-driven (value already shows on screen). Prototype the split-turn prompt against probe_tool_call.py (target 5/5 on 3.1) before touching the live confirm flow. May touch backend/config.py (SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION + confirmation_policy) and possibly the confirm sequencing in callback_handler/ai_context.

title: Infinite confirm_field / next_field_hint_response loop when a field can't be confirmed
description: Demo console shows a tight loop on p1_line1_aliennumber: Confirming field -> computeNextField -> Section completion check (allFieldsConfirmed: false, nextFieldInCurrentSection = same field) -> next_field_hint_response -> (backend re-requests) -> Confirming field ... forever, while Gemini stops responding. Mechanism: confirmField (schemaFormState.ts:786) no-ops when the field has no value, so computeNextField(skipConfirmed:true) keeps returning the SAME field, the frontend keeps answering the backend's next-field/confirm requests with the same unconfirmed field, and nothing advances. handleConfirmFieldRequest (webFormConnection.ts:945) has no guard against re-confirming an already-targeted-but-unfillable field. title: WS reconnect drops auth token -> 403 on post-disclaimer first-section connect
description: Root cause: webFormConnection.connect(wsUrl, timeoutMs, token?) only appends ?token= when a token arg is passed, and the token is never stored on the instance. Reconnect paths call connect() with no token: startSection() at line ~1476 (the post-disclaimer switchToFirstSection reconnect) and attemptReconnect() at line ~1089 (auto-reconnect backoff). connectedUrl is stored as the bare URL (token not baked in). Result: every reconnect hits backend /ws/fill auth gate (websocket_routes.py verify_token) with no token -> HTTP 403 in ~20ms -> browser surfaces 1006 -> tokenless retries also 403. Confirmed in Cloud Run logs (6x GET /ws/fill 403) and frontend console (5 reconnect attempts, code 1006). Latent since auth layer aa66f45 (2026-01-21); disclaimer->first-section is the first reconnect to exercise it. Fix: connection holds a getToken callback (auth.currentUser.getIdToken()) and fetches a fresh token before EVERY (re)connect, with the original token cached as fallback. Refresh-on-reconnect also covers ~1h Firebase ID token expiry on long sessions.

title: Gate 2: runtime efficiency -- Neo4j vs dict on our queries
description:
GATE 2 of the feasibility-gated spike. Only run if Gate 1 (hi2.1) passes.

Question: even if the data has graph structure, is a graph ENGINE efficient for
how we actually query it? Graph DBs win at deep/variable-depth traversal; they are
frequently SLOWER than a hash map for shallow point lookups. Our real access
patterns (from baseline research) are mostly 1-2 hop: get field by id, get a
section's fields, what does field X control / what controls X, look up a prior
field's value.

Method: model I-90 in real Neo4j (Docker) AND a plain indexed dict/JSON.
Benchmark BOTH on the identical query set -- latency + code complexity per query.
Honest hypothesis to TEST (not confirm): our queries are shallow, dict is O(1),
Neo4j's planner overhead loses.

KILL CONDITION: if a dict matches/beats Neo4j on our actual query shapes, the
graph-engine-at-runtime option is dead -- STOP before any cost build. Record
separately whether Gate-1 graph-shapedness still makes a graph a better AUTHORING
model (non-runtime finding).

Done = latency + code-complexity table (Neo4j vs dict) on the named queries +
explicit kill-condition verdict. Blocked by Gate 1; blocks Gate 3.
acceptance_criteria: Working prototype performs >=3 distinct tool-call traversals end-to-end over the WS. Recorded table: tokens, median/p95 per-hop latency, total session duration -- graph-traversal vs legacy baseline on the same form. Explicit verdict on the 'token-cheaper but latency-worse' hypothesis with the numbers behind it.
notes: FRESH-EYES (corrects baseline): get_form_status/get_field_value ALREADY round-trip to the client over the WS today (callback_handler.py -> request_form_state_from_client). The graph design does NOT introduce the client hop -- it changes the hop COUNT per field. Measure against TWO baselines: (i) existing single-tool-call round-trip (get_form_status) = apples-to-apples; (ii) legacy full-schema path. The bet is the delta in client-hop count per field, not the existence of the hop.
close_reason: Obviated by Gate 1 (hi2.1): runtime-graph rejected for I-90; Neo4j-vs-dict benchmark never runs. Spike pivoting to PDF->JSON authoring.

title: Gate 1: structural fit -- is I-90 actually graph-shaped?
description:
GATE 1 of the feasibility-gated spike (cheapest kill-point; no Docker/Neo4j needed).

Question: is I-90's form data actually graph-shaped, or a tree wearing a graph
costume? A form is mostly a tree (Form->Parts->Sections->Fields) which JSON
nesting expresses natively -- a graph only earns its keep on edges that BREAK the
tree (cross-cutting links).

Method: analyze form-kits/i-90/schema.json (132 fields). Classify every
relationship as TREE (containment) vs CROSS-LINK (show_if/controls_fields that
point ACROSS sections, overflow_to_supplement, copy_to/conditional_fields,
conditional_behavior). Compute the ratio. Known counts: 19 show_if, 13
controls_fields, 16 conditional_behavior, 0 hide_if. Open question: how many are
GENUINELY cross-section vs intra-section (JSON handles intra-section trivially).
Also catalog the ~40 FormField attributes (read form_models.py with explicit
UTF-8): structural-edge vs imperative/behavioral (not graph-shaped at all).

KILL CONDITION: if I-90 is overwhelmingly tree (cross-links rare/mostly intra-
section), a graph is the wrong tool -- STOP, write up the negative result. This
gate can end the whole effort cheaply.

Done = tree-vs-cross-link ratio table + full attribute classification + explicit
kill-condition verdict. Blocks Gate 2.
acceptance_criteria: Throwaway graph artifact for one full real form, cross-checked field-for-field against its existing schema (mapped/unmapped counts recorded). The 'doesn't map cleanly' list enumerated with the modeling gap noted per item. The show_if/controls_fields collapse shown concretely on at least one real conditional.
notes: FRESH-EYES: (1) FIRST pick the canonical ground-truth schema file -- I-589 has THREE on disk (i589_schema.json, i589_rich_schema_with_tu.json, i589_internal_structure.json); name the one hi2.4 scores against. (2) The doesn't-map-cleanly set is a DISCOVERY task, not an exhaustive pre-seed -- FormField has ~25-30 non-ID-reference attributes; 'done' = the FULL non-mapping set enumerated, not just the seed list confirmed.
close_reason: Gate 1 complete: I-90 analyzed, 0 of 62 field->field conditional edges genuinely cross-section -> tree-shaped -> runtime-graph REJECTED. Finding in docs/journal/entries/2026-06-06-bd-hi2.1-gate1-structural-fit.md. Lesson in bd remember graph-fit-by-cross-cutting-edge-ratio.

title: Epic: Graph-based form representation (client-hydrated, LLM-traversable) -- research spike
description:
Research/exploration spike (NOT shipped code). Decide adopt / adopt-partially /
reject / defer for two separable sub-problems around representing forms as a
graph instead of the current hand-authored JSON FormSchema:

- Problem A -- Authoring/ingestion: PDF -> graph structure via Document AI Form
  Parser + Gemini structuring. Offline, pre-deployment, never sees user values --
  invariant-clean. The real bottleneck (no extraction pipeline exists today).
- Problem B -- Runtime representation: a graph the client HYDRATES (values in
  sessionStorage) and the LLM traverses via tool calls, replacing the legacy
  flattened-section handshake. Make-or-break is a round-trip-per-hop topology:
  the LLM runs server-side, the value-bearing graph must live client-side (PII
  invariant), so each traversal is backend->client->backend over the WS,
  mid-voice-session, billed on Gemini Live session DURATION. Token-cheaper but
  latency-worse is the likely failure mode.

OUT OF BOUNDS (record as rejected): storing filled VALUES server-side -- breaks
the stateless-backend invariant (docs/standards/stateless-architecture.md) and
HIPAA/PII policy (docs/standards/hipaa-pii-policy.md).

Deliverable: a measured recommendation as a journal entry + throwaway prototypes.

Working hypothesis: A is a likely high-value invariant-clean win (file a follow-on
implementation bead); B likely "adopt-partially" -- adopt the graph MODEL, but the
runtime-traversal-over-WS piece probably loses on voice latency.

Children: model (foundation) -> {traverse, compile-back, client-weight};
ingestion (parallel Problem A track); recommend (gates on all measurement beads).
Full session plan: .claude/plans/let-s-expand-this-some-luminous-riddle.md
acceptance_criteria: All child measurement beads closed with recorded numbers. A journal entry under docs/journal/entries/ carries the per-sub-problem recommendation citing the standards/architecture docs. Follow-on implementation beads (if any sub-problem scores adopt) are filed and linked, not built here.
notes: Full plan committed to repo (remote-session-readable): docs/journal/entries/2026-06-05-bd-hi2-graph-form-representation-spike-plan.md
close_reason: Exploration complete with a clear verdict: a graph is NOT the right representation for polyglot-pdf forms. Gate 1 (hi2.1) found I-90 tree-shaped (0 of 62 conditional edges cross-section); runtime-graph rejected at the cheapest gate, Gates 2-3 obviated. The real pain -- PDF->schema authoring cost -- is representation-agnostic and continues under a fresh epic targeting PDF->JSON FormSchema. Findings: journal 2026-06-06-bd-hi2.1; lesson: bd remember graph-fit-by-cross-cutting-edge-ratio.

title: [bug] Live API compression eviction did not bound prompt_tokens in 45o sweep (gemini-3.1 native-audio)
description:
The 45o window-size sweep (scripts/spikes/sweep_compression_window.py + _findings.md, run 2026-06-04) measured that enabling ContextWindowCompressionConfig did NOT bound billed prompt_token_count on gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview: across triggers 5000 and 2000, prompt_tokens climbed monotonically 10x-14x over 12 audio turns with NO eviction even when the prompt clearly exceeded trigger_tokens (window-1500/trigger-2000 run: turn 8 prompt=2041, turn 12=3395, never dropped back toward 1500). Cumulative cost stayed super-linear. The config IS reaching the wire correctly (verified offline: adapter raw dict serializes to triggerTokens/slidingWindow/targetTokens), so this is semantic, not a wiring bug. This blocks the cost win the l3a epic is premised on -- the compression code is wired + tested + reversible (CONTEXT_COMPRESSION_ENABLED, default False) but NOT validated as delivering cost reduction.

Open hypotheses (NOT verified -- do not assume): (a) eviction may only manifest over longer sessions than a 12-turn probe; (b) usage_metadata prompt_token_count may not reflect eviction; (c) this native-audio preview model may not honor contextWindowCompression like the docs' general example. A text probe to isolate (a)/(b) is impossible -- the model rejects TEXT modality (1007, native-audio emits AUDIO only). Next steps: longer-session audio run (drive past more turns / higher accumulation); check raw usage_metadata fields beyond prompt_token_count; consult genai_docs / Google for native-audio compression semantics; consider testing on a cascade model if one supports it. Keep ENABLED=False until resolved.
notes: ROOT CAUSE FOUND (2026-06-04): contextWindowCompression is a SILENT NO-OP on every native-audio Live model reachable on this key. Config serializes correctly + server ACCEPTS it (no rejection across triggers 200-4096), but NO eviction: prompt_token_count crosses the trigger and compounds ~7x exactly as compression-off, on BOTH gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview and gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-12-2025, IDENTICALLY under v1alpha and v1beta. Ruled out: bad syntax, API rejection, api_version, model-specificity. UNTESTABLE here: cascade Live models (gemini-live-2.5-flash-preview etc.) all 1008 'not found for bidiGenerateContent'; models.list() shows only native-audio. Docs' compression example uses a cascade model -> compression likely not implemented for native-audio yet (documented-but-not-live for our family). Diagnostics: scripts/spikes/diag_compression_{apiversion,connect_boundary,cascade,usage}.py + l3a1_compression_rootcause_findings.md. Stored as bd memory compression-noop-on-native-audio-live + genai_docs/README hard-won fact. REMAINING (why this stays open as a watch-item, not closed): the one branch we could not test is whether compression evicts on a CASCADE Live model -- needs a key/project with cascade access. If/when available, run diag_compression_cascade.py to confirm native-audio-gap vs broadly-inert. CONTEXT_COMPRESSION_ENABLED stays False; config is plumbed for a zero-code-change enable if Google ships native-audio eviction.

title: [P1][SECURITY] Production logs leak PII/PHI: field values + user transcript at INFO -> Cloud Run/BigQuery
description:
Found 2026-05-30 while writing the hipaa-pii-policy doc (b11). The repo's stated policy is 'NEVER log field values/PII/PHI', but several INFO/WARNING-level logs emit actual user data to stdout -> Cloud Run -> BigQuery (per the logging pipeline). For an immigration-form app (A-numbers, names, addresses, DOB), these are real HIPAA/PII violations in PRODUCTION (INFO/WARNING are always emitted, not gated by debug).

CONFIRMED LEAKS (verified against code 2026-05-30):
1. backend/routes/pdf_fill_routes.py:52 — _log.info('pdf_fill_sample_values', kit=..., sample=sample_values) logs the FIRST 5 field_id:VALUE pairs. Comment even says 'DEBUG: Log first 5 field values to verify data is coming through' but it's at INFO. CRITICAL.
2. backend/adapters/live_ai_gemini.py:902 — text_preview=transcription.text[:50] logs the first 50 chars of Gemini's transcript of USER SPEECH (e.g. 'My alien number is A012...'). INFO level. CRITICAL.
3. backend/routes/pdf_fill_routes.py — additional value logging at INFO/WARNING: line 249 warning(value=value), 326 info(selected_values=value), 341 info(selected_value=selected_value), 387 warning(value=value); plus DEBUG-level ones (120/123/126/295/375) that leak if LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG.

SAFE (verified, no action): confirmation_logger.py (ids/names/methods only, explicit NO-PII), token_file_logger.py (counts/costs), frontend metrics.ts (local-only, never transmitted), log_schemas.py (TypedDict excludes values, comment 'NEVER include field values!'), disclaimer_routes.py (session/lang/ts + ip/user_agent — fingerprinting concern, not PHI). dev_file_logger.py intentionally logs PHI but gated by .env.DEV (gitignored, absent in prod containers) — acceptable but document the gate.

FIX: remove/redact the value+transcript logs (log field_id + value_length/type/hash, never the value or text_preview). Audit ALL _log.* calls in pdf_fill_routes.py and live_ai_gemini.py for value/text leakage. Consider a structlog processor that strips known-sensitive keys (value/selected_value/target_value/text_preview/sample) as defense-in-depth. The hipaa-pii-policy.md doc (b11) will codify the never-log/always-safe rules; THIS bead fixes the code to match. Acceptance: no field value or transcript text reaches stdout at any level used in prod; a test asserts the structured log of a fill/transcript contains no value; confirm via a grep gate in CI if feasible.
close_reason: Stale-open: fix merged. PR #26 (fix/hjo-pii-log-leaks) MERGED 2026-05-30 (commit de2d8b0). Verified on dev: both CRITICAL leaks gone — pdf_fill_routes.py now logs sample_field_ids/value_length/value_type (not values, all marked '# never log value -- bd hjo'); live_ai_gemini.py transcript log now uses text_length not text_preview. Acceptance test backend/tests/test_no_pii_logging.py exists (AST guard over the sensitive files + test_guard_catches_known_leaks asserting the two original leaks are caught) and PASSES 3/3. Bead left in_progress after merge under the old hold-until-merge pattern. Audit 2026-06-01.

title: copilot_watch.py: false-COMMENTS loop — re-surfaces stale round-1 inline comment after Copilot resolves via issue-comment
description:
DIAGNOSED via multi-agent workflow against live PR #21 data (2026-05-30). copilot_watch.py reported RESULT: COMMENTS on every re-watch even after Copilot's GitHub thread explicitly said 'no further changes were needed' — an infinite false-positive loop that blocks /closeout from ever reaching CLEAN.

THREE COMPOUNDING BUGS (A is primary):

BUG A (PRIMARY) — surface mismatch. _latest_copilot_review (lines 201-231) reads /pulls/{pr}/reviews ONLY. On PR 21 Copilot emitted exactly one formal REVIEW (4395801885, state=COMMENTED @19:00:31Z); its round-2 'no changes needed' verdicts (@19:08, @19:10) were ISSUE COMMENTS (no state, no review_id, never appear in /reviews). So the selector can only ever return the frozen round-1 review. The verdict surface (/reviews) and resolution surface (/issues/.../comments) are never reconciled.

BUG B — inline comments matched by review_id never expire. _collect_findings (lines 294-302, match at 297) re-attaches review 4395801885's inline comment 3329167386 forever. That comment has position:null / line:null (anchor fell out of the diff = GitHub's canonical 'outdated' signal), but line 299 LAUNDERS the null (c.get('line') or c.get('original_line') or '?') instead of treating it as staleness -> re-emitted as a live finding -> _emit('COMMENTS').

BUG C — SKILL invokes watcher without --since. SKILL.md line 106 (round-1) and line 126 (re-watch) both call 'copilot_watch.py <pr#>' bare. --since defaults None, _after() short-circuits True (186-187), no round floor -> round-1 'reviewed' event + review re-detected every run.

KEY INSIGHT: fixing C alone converts false-COMMENTS into false-TIMEOUT (since-floor excludes the only review -> None -> polls to TIMEOUT, because the real verdict is in issue-comments it never reads). Must fix A+B1+C together.

FIX (land together):
- Fix B1 (necessary): in inline loop ~295-302, 'if c.get("position") is None: continue' (drop outdated). Keep state-in-NON_CLEAN_STATES checks (370,383) ABOVE the drop so CHANGES_REQUESTED still wins.
- Fix A (necessary): when timeline=reviewed but _latest_copilot_review returns None, classify from Copilot ISSUE COMMENTS at/after since (default to COMMENTS unless a tight approval pattern matches — err toward more review, never read silence/ambiguity as CLEAN).
- SKILL --since (necessary): capture server-authoritative created_at of the re-trigger comment ('TS=') and pass --since "" on the re-watch (line 126). Round-1 watch (106) stays bare (no prior round).
- Fix B2 (nice-to-have, defer): GraphQL reviewThreads isResolved/outdated to catch resolved-but-in-diff threads.

TESTS to add (tests/ has copilot_watch tests): (1) COMMENTED review + position:null inline -> CLEAN; (2) issue-comment-only round (reviews has only pre-since review -> None) + 'no further changes' issue comment -> CLEAN not TIMEOUT; (3) --since excludes round-1 events; (4) NEGATIVE: live round-2 inline w/ non-null position -> still COMMENTS; CHANGES_REQUESTED w/ only position:null comment -> still COMMENTS (state wins).

RISK addressed: dropping position:null can't hide a genuine round-2 finding (those land on the current diff w/ non-null position); ambiguous issue comments default to COMMENTS. Full synthesis in workflow output. This is a claude-swarm-kit script bug — affects every repo using the kit's closeout.
close_reason: Merged-ready via PR #24. Fixed the copilot_watch.py false-COMMENTS loop: (A) classify issue-comment re-review verdicts, (B) drop position-null outdated inline comments, (C) SKILL passes --since on re-watch. Hardened per fresh-eyes+Copilot: _is_approval_comment rejects mixed comments, _latest_by_created by timestamp, approvals not counted as findings. CRITICAL save: both reviewers caught that the first commit had reverted bead 39a's Windows UTF-8 guard (stale-base cp clobber) — rebuilt from dev and restored it + tests. Dogfooded: PR #24's own --since re-watch returned CLEAN. 36 watcher tests + 149 suite pass; real PR #21 shape verified (without --since COMMENTS, with --since CLEAN).

title: [P1] form_filling_service.py syntax-broken on dev+main (botched merge dup) — crashes /ws/fill
description:
backend/services/form_filling_service.py does NOT parse (SyntaxError at line ~224) on BOTH origin/dev and origin/main. Root cause: merge 2966c48 ('Merge branch shared-audio-stream and resolve conflicts') resolved a conflict by KEEPING BOTH SIDES, duplicating lines in send_disclaimer_message() (~lines 210-230): the docstring 'disclaimer_text:' line, the 'if not self._live_ai' guard, the DISCLAIMER_INITIATING_MESSAGE.format() kwargs (spoken_language/disclaimer_text appear twice inside one call -> the actual SyntaxError), and the _log.info line. No raw conflict markers remain (both sides kept, markers deleted).

BLAST RADIUS / why it wasn't caught: dependencies.py:30 imports FormFillingService LAZILY (inside get_form_filling_service factory, not at module top), so 'import backend.main' succeeds and the app boots. But the factory runs on the FIRST /ws/fill connection (websocket_routes.py:560 Depends(get_form_filling_service)) -> that request would crash on the un-parseable module. So this is a latent P1 on the core voice form-fill path, not dead code. ALSO: because the file can't be imported, the entire backend/tests/ suite fails at COLLECTION (any test importing FormFillingService), which is why od1's idle-timeout asserts (and likely many others) silently don't run.

FIX: de-duplicate send_disclaimer_message() to one copy of each line (keep the .format() with each kwarg once). Then: (1) py_compile/ast.parse the whole file clean; (2) confirm 'import backend.services.form_filling_service' succeeds; (3) re-run backend/tests/ and see how many tests now COLLECT (expect a jump) — triage any that then fail. 

PROD-REALITY QUESTION (open): main is broken too, so either prod is deployed from a different artifact/branch, or live /ws/fill is currently erroring on disclaimer send. Confirm what prod actually runs before assuming severity. NOTE the duplication may not be the only conflict-kept-both-sides damage from 2966c48 — the parser halts at the first error, so after fixing, re-scan the file (and other files that merge touched: VoiceOverlay, LanguageSelectionModal per the commit msg) for the same kept-both-sides pattern. Surfaced 2026-05-30 while investigating od1 from the PR #16 docs review.

- pytest --co: 149 tests collect, 0 collection errors (was 120 collected + 5 collection ERRORS pre-fix). The 5 files that could not collect -- test_disclaimer_flow, test_empty_tool_call_validation, test_idle_timeout, test_jit_schema_loading, test_section_switching -- now collect. +29 tests.

title: Explore SPEAR workflow model (Scope, Plan, Execute, Assess, Resolve) as upgrade to current workflow
description:
## Goal

Research and evaluate the SPEAR workflow model as a potential upgrade to the current beads-based sprint workflow.

## SPEAR phases

- **Scope** -- define the work boundary, success criteria, and what is explicitly out of scope before touching any code
- **Plan** -- break scope into ordered steps, identify blockers and dependencies, choose approach
- **Execute** -- implement the plan with a tight feedback loop
- **Assess** -- review what was built against the scope criteria; identify gaps, regressions, or drift
- **Resolve** -- close out cleanly: fix assessment gaps, update docs, file follow-on beads, merge

## Questions to answer

1. How does SPEAR map onto the existing bead + closeout lifecycle?
2. Which phases are already covered (e.g. Plan ~ current pre-bead scoping, Execute ~ current sprint, Resolve ~ closeout)?
3. Where are the gaps? (Scope gating before claiming a bead? Assess step before /closeout?)
4. Would adding explicit Scope and Assess checkpoints reduce rework and escalation?
5. What would the CLAUDE.md / workflow.md changes look like?
6. Are there tradeoffs (overhead vs. quality, token cost, maintainer burden)?

## Deliverable

A short recommendation doc (or journal entry) with: current-state mapping, gap analysis, a proposed SPEAR-augmented workflow sketch, and a verdict (adopt / adopt-partially / defer). File follow-on beads for any agreed changes to workflow docs.

title: fix(harness_ledger): append guards against a missing trailing newline (JSONL corruption)
description:
harness_ledger.py:296-297 appends a row as  in 'a' mode. This is correct ONLY if the file already ends in a newline. If a prior writer left NO trailing newline, the new row concatenates onto the last line, producing two JSON objects on one physical line -> the file is no longer valid JSONL (json.loads on that line raises 'Extra data').

OBSERVED on PR #144 closeout (2026-06-10): the PR #141 row (wpw.2/p84m) ended without a trailing newline, so closeout_finish.py's PR #144 telemetry append glued the cd0 row onto it (line 72: ...errors_shipped: 0}{recorded_at...). Caught by BOTH fresh-eyes AND Codex as a P1 blocker. Hand-fixed in the PR #144 branch (split the line + ensured a trailing newline), but the SCRIPT will reproduce this whenever the file lacks a final newline.

FIX: before writing, ensure the file ends with a newline -- e.g. open in 'a+', seek to end, and if the last byte is not chr(10) (and the file is non-empty), write a leading newline before the row; OR always write chr(10)+json.dumps(row) and strip a leading blank line on read; OR rewrite-with-newline-normalize. Add a tiny unit test that appends to a file with no trailing newline and asserts the result parses as JSONL. Whichever PR #141 left the bad state is incidental; the durable fix is the append guard. Surfaces: scripts/harness_ledger.py (the append at ~296).
notes: FIXED. append_row (scripts/harness_ledger.py) now prepends a newline via a new _needs_leading_newline(path) helper when the existing file is non-empty and does NOT end in chr(10) -- self-healing the exact state that corrupted PR #144 (a prior writer's missing trailing newline would otherwise glue the next row onto the last line -> invalid JSONL). Cheap final-byte seek; empty/missing files get no prefix. Three regression tests added to TestAppendRow: self-heals-missing-newline (proven to FAIL without the fix with the same 'Extra data' JSONDecodeError), no-double-newline on the happy path, and no-leading-blank-line on an empty file. 32 harness_ledger tests + 411 tests/ pass. NOTE: 2 PRE-EXISTING non-ASCII chars (section-sign at harness_ledger.py:5,346, in docstrings) are out of scope here -- flagged separately.
close_reason: OBSOLETE -- superseded by rtfn (PR #142, merged to dev). That change moved harness telemetry from a shared-append harness_ledger.jsonl to one .json file PER ROW under docs/journal/telemetry/. The missing-trailing-newline -> JSON-concatenation bug cpx8 fixes is STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE in the per-row model (no shared append target; the legacy JSONL is now read-only). The cpx8 append_row newline-guard + its 3 tests targeted the old single-file append, which no longer exists on dev. title: BUG: native-audio update_form_fields FunctionResponse missing id -> send_tool_response raises, breaks turn continuation
description:
Found by the g8w E2E voice harness on its first live run (worktree off dev, 2.5 native-audio model). Cycle: injected scripted audio 'one two three four five six seven' -> Gemini transcribed it -> update_form_fields tool_call -> field p1_line1_aliennumber correctly filled with '1234567' (PASS). But immediately after, backend raised:

ValueError: FunctionResponse request must have an 'id' field from the response of a ToolCall.FunctionalCalls

Root cause: in the model_turn.parts[].function_call path, the function_call can arrive with NO id (native-audio 2.5). At live_ai_gemini.py:1437-1438 the FunctionResponse id is set ONLY 'if call_id', so a missing id yields a FunctionResponse without id, which send_tool_response() rejects (google-genai live.py:416, _FUNCTION_RESPONSE_REQUIRES_ID). Note the contradictory comment at :1536 ('FunctionResponse should NOT include id') vs the SDK now REQUIRING it -- likely interacts with the just-merged polyglot-pdf-tks tool_response fix. Likely needs: synthesize/propagate a stable id for the model_turn path, or use the event.tool_call path's id. Repro: run tests/e2e/voice-harness RUNBOOK against a worktree backend on dev.

title: BUG: switch_section orphans its own tool_response -- handler cancels the receive task before the FunctionResponse is sent
description:
switch_section is the one tool whose tool_response is NOT reliably delivered to Gemini, because the handler tears down the very task that would send it. Lower urgency than the first-tool-call loop (covered under polyglot-pdf-tks #1/#2, fixed) -- section switching is mid-form, not the blocking first turn.

THE DEFECT (verified by static trace 2026-06-08):
1. Gemini -> switch_section -> adapter on_tool_call -> callback_handler._handle_switch_section_tool -> form_filling_service.handle_switch_section -> AWAITS switch_to_section() INLINE (form_filling_service.py L847).
2. switch_to_section calls self._live_ai.finalize() (form_filling_service.py L580).
3. finalize() does self._bg_task.cancel() (live_ai_gemini.py L603). That bg task IS the 'async for event in session.receive()' loop (L1108) currently RUNNING this switch_section callback. So the receive loop cancels itself from inside its own tool callback.
4. The downstream code that appends the FunctionResponse (live_ai_gemini.py ~L1418-1440) and calls session.send_tool_response (~L1565) is on that same now-cancelled task, pointed at the OLD session finalize() just closed. The switch_section call gets NO response on the session that issued it.

WHY IT USUALLY 'WORKS': switch_to_section -> start_session opens a NEW session that re-sends the system instruction + initial_field_hint and re-greets ('Waiting for user to speak'). Gemini proceeds driven by the NEW session, not by a response to her switch_section call. It HANGS when that new-session turn-start does not fire cleanly: token re-fetch fails, no greeting/turn injected, or native-VAD waits on user audio that never comes -> Gemini sits with an unanswered switch_section call and silence.

FIX OPTIONS (design call):
(a) PREFERRED -- send the switch_section FunctionResponse on the OLD session BEFORE finalize(): have the adapter flush the tool_response for switch_section prior to the section teardown (defer finalize until after send_tool_response). Most faithful to the Live API contract (every call gets a response on its own session).
(b) Make switch_section non-blocking: return the tool response immediately, then perform the session swap asynchronously (after the response is on the wire).
(c) Adapter special-cases switch_section: append + send_tool_response, THEN allow the swap.

VERIFY FIRST: capture one real switch_section round-trip with the kbf dev-logging (backend/logs/gemini_<date>.jsonl). Look for a tool_call (path=model_turn.parts or event.tool_call) for switch_section with NO following tool_response on that session id, then a session_open for the next section. That confirms the orphaned-response timing before changing teardown ordering.

Context: split out of the polyglot-pdf-tks round-trip audit (see its comments). #1/#2 (adapter parts-path dropping the FunctionResponse on missing id / callback exception) are FIXED in the tks PR; this #3 is the remaining, higher-effort one.
close_reason: Closed by PR #135 (bd 0c1, which absorbed it): the switch_section orphaned-tool-response race is fixed -- the handler now returns the response payload immediately (delivered on the old session via the cooperative flush point) and swaps on a detached task, instead of awaiting finalize() inline and cancelling its own receive task.

title: Perfect checkbox/radio round-trip (preserve the I-90 convention) + true fill-back harness
description:
RESEARCH + IMPLEMENTATION. Perfect checkbox/radio round-trip in the extracted FormSchema -- the genuinely hard case, and the one the current bake-off does NOT verify. Choice fields are 18% of I-90 (24/132) and 25% of I-589 (40/156): a large, high-value surface, not an edge case.

WHY IT IS NOT COVERED TODAY: the bake-off scorer (scripts/schema_score.py) never opens the PDF or writes a value -- it matches on pdf_field_name and grades type/options as SOFT attributes. A schema can score green on names yet FAIL a real fill. For text fields the name+type proxy is sound; for checkbox/radio it is NOT, because the filler selects the widget by matching the VALUE the app sends against option.value, then fills option.pdf_field_name. The 7a9.9 LLM-native prototype scored options 0-16% on I-90 -- so even at 100% widget-name accuracy, choice groups can silently fail to fill.

PRESERVE THE HARD-WON I-90 CONVENTION (we worked hard to make this exact shape work; treat it as the spec a new extractor must REPRODUCE, and as round-trip regression cases). Verified in form-kits/i-90/schema.json + backend/routes/pdf_fill_routes.py + frontend/src/schema-forms/components/fields/{RadioField,CheckboxField}.tsx:

1. CANONICAL option.value == the WIDGET LEAF IDENTIFIER, never a semantic label. I-90 radio options use value "P1_checkbox4[0]" (the widget leaf), NOT "Yes". This is the join key end-to-end:
   - RadioField.tsx sets the field value to option.value (input value={option.value} -> onChange(e.target.value)).
   - the filler matches `opt.get("value") == value` (pdf_fill_routes.py ~line 247/329) and fills option.pdf_field_name.
   - controls_fields[].value references the SAME widget-leaf string (e.g. {"operator":"equals","value":"P1_checkbox4[0]","unlocks":[...]}), so conditional logic fires off the same convention. An extractor that invents semantic values breaks selection AND conditionals at once.
2. A "radio" field has pdf_field_name=None at FIELD level; the name lives ONLY on each option.pdf_field_name. Consolidation must put each widget's EXACT full name on its option.
3. A logical radio can span DIFFERENT widget names, not just indices of one: I-90 p1_line8_male is type radio with options P1_Line8_male[0] AND P1_Line8_female[0] (two distinct widgets presented as one choice). Consolidation must group by MEANING, not by shared leaf base.
4. VALUE SHAPES the filler/frontend expect (round-trip must produce schemas that match these):
   - radio -> a single option.value (widget leaf string).
   - checkbox WITH options (multi-select) -> a string[] of option.value (CheckboxField.tsx handleToggle/newValues; filler iterates the list).
   - single checkbox (NO options) -> a boolean; uses field-level pdf_field_name (p2_checkbox3 still carries a 1-element options[] AND a field-level pdf_field_name -- preserve that dual shape).
5. The checkbox "on" appearance state is derived LIVE by the filler from widget.button_states() (pdf_fill_routes.py ~line 83), so on_value in the schema is informational -- round-trip must NOT depend on the extractor getting on_value right (but capture it for debugging).
6. READ-ONLY choice widgets unlock via BOTH keys the schema carries together: conditional_behavior.unlock_method="flip_readonly_bit" AND conditional_logic.pdf_field_flag_change={bit,current_value,required_value} (see I-90 p2_checkbox2[5], p2_checkbox3). The filler reads conditional_behavior.pdf_field_flag_change (apply_field_flag_changes, ~line 176). 0% of bake-off arms populate this -- any read-only checkbox won't fill. Reproduce both keys.
7. Field ids can carry a widget index (p2_checkbox2[5], p3_checkbox4[1]); ids are extractor-chosen and matching never trusts them, but do not let a generated id collide.

DELIVERABLES:
- A TRUE round-trip harness (throwaway, scripts/bakeoff/): feed an arm's schema + a synthetic full-coverage value set (using the value SHAPES in #4) through the actual fill_pdf logic, re-open the saved PDF, and assert each targeted widget received its value (AS for checkbox/radio, field_value for text). Emit a HARD per-arm choice_fill_success = filled/attempted for checkbox+radio SPECIFICALLY (separate from text). Use the I-90 gold schema as the round-trip regression baseline -- it MUST score ~100% (it is the known-good shape).
- The canonical option.value convention (#1) documented + enforced in the schema contract (scripts/bakeoff/schema_contract.py) and the LLM-native arm prompt (arm_llm_native.py), with the multi-widget-radio (#3) and read-only-unlock (#6) rules called out as few-shot.
- Extractor changes in the generic-enrichment LLM-native pass so checkbox/radio consolidation + option.value + option.pdf_field_name + value-shape + read-only-unlock reach a target choice_fill_success on I-90 AND I-589.
- Recommendation: does the round-trip harness become a PERMANENT bake-off gate?

RELATION: surfaced during 7a9.9 (docs/research/2026-06-07-7a9.9-llm-native-extractor-prototype-findings.md, Q5). This GATES 7a9.12 (adopt + retire heuristics) for the choice-field case -- do not retire the heuristics until checkbox/radio prove a real round-trip fill matching the I-90 convention above. Coordinate the option.value convention with 7a9.13 (section_id metric decision); both touch schema conventions.
