title: DECISION: section_id scoring is a seeding artifact -- pick grouping vs convention-as-canon
description:
DECISION / PRODUCT CALL (surfaced by 7a9.9; maintainer owns this). The schema scorer (scripts/schema_score.py) grades section_id by EXACT STRING MATCH. The 7a9.9 prototype proved this metric is broken: on I-90 EVERY arm including the deterministic extractor scores section_id 0.0%; the deterministic arm's 88.3% is I-589-ONLY and is an artifact of the I-589 gold schema having been authored by editing that extractor's output. The I-90 gold section_id strings are internally inconsistent hand-authored noise ('Part 1 - Information About You' mixed with 'part_1_2_addresses'), so no extractor can match them and no convention is learnable. Meanwhile the LLM PRODUCES clean, consistent section ids (part_1_info, part_6_interpreter_address) -- arguably better than gold.

THE CALL (maintainer): either (a) adopt the LLM's generated section_id convention as canon and regenerate/relabel the gold schemas to it, OR (b) change the scorer to grade section GROUPING (which fields share a section) instead of the exact id string, OR (c) leave it and ignore section_id as a quality signal. This affects how we measure every future authoring arm.

DELIVERABLE: a decision, then the scorer and/or gold schemas updated to match it. Until decided, section_id stays excluded from the headline quality judgment (per the 7a9.9 recommendation).

title: Adopt generic-enrichment LLM-native authoring pass; retire USCIS heuristics
description:
IMPLEMENTATION (depends on the 7a9.9 research + the ablation + the I-589 validation). Adopt the generic-enrichment LLM-native pass as the PDF->JSON authoring engine and RETIRE the USCIS-specific heuristic interpretation layer (heuristic_hierarchy_parser.py tooltip parsing + extractor.py section-id/field-semantics).

BASIS (7a9.9 findings, docs/research/2026-06-07-7a9.9-llm-native-extractor-prototype-findings.md): the generic-enrichment pass (acroform_dump.py exact-name anchor + structural_enrich.py generic signals + a strong LLM) matches/beats the hybrid on (a) field detection + typing with ZERO form-specific code, and degrades gracefully on the tooltip-less W-7 where the heuristic produces nothing. KEEP acroform_dump.py (the anti-hallucination exact-name anchor); retire the interpretation heuristics.

RELATION TO 7a9.8: this RESHAPES 7a9.8 ("fused deterministic-skeleton -> LLM (b) pass"). The 7a9.9 finding is that the deterministic SKELETON's interpretation half (section_id, field semantics) is not worth keeping -- the LLM does it better from generic signals. Reconcile with 7a9.8 before building (they may merge, or 7a9.8 becomes this).

MODEL: claude-opus-4-8 via the local claude CLI (free in maintainer's environment; schema extraction runs in-env). Keep the gemini-* SDK path wired as a selectable fallback for hired help. Both already pluggable via arm_llm_native.py --model.

DELIVERABLES: the production authoring pass (not throwaway); add it as a SCORED bake-off arm (manifest.json + harness) per the 7a9.9 integration note; the retired heuristic modules removed or quarantined; recommendation reconciled with 7a9.8.

WHY THIS IS THE RISK CASE: (Q5) I-589 has 9 tables where claude-hybrid beat gemini 7/9 vs 0/9 -- does the enriched bundle help consolidation? (Q6) gemini-3.1-pro TIMED OUT on the 460-widget single-shot hybrid call in the bake-off; the enriched bundle is ~26% LARGER, so big-form chunking matters MORE. Test whether Opus 4.8 via the local CLI completes the single-shot call, and if not, design a page/part-chunked pass.

title: RESEARCH: per-signal ablation of the generic structural-enrichment pass

The 7a9.9 prototype showed the bundle AS A WHOLE lifts I-90 field typing 85.5% -> ~96% and F1 97.0 -> 98.5 over the plain hybrid, but did NOT isolate which signal does the work.

title: RESEARCH: LLM-native extractor architecture (retire USCIS heuristics, feed LLM all structural signals)
description:
Parallel research branch (maintainer will run a separate session). Full proposal: docs/research/2026-06-07-llm-native-extractor-architecture.md -- READ IT FIRST; it has the known facts, the hypothesized architecture, open questions Q1-Q7, the falsifiable hypothesis, and cold-start file pointers.

THESIS: the deterministic extractor's 'intelligence' layer (heuristic_hierarchy_parser.py + extractor.py section-id/field-semantics) is reverse-engineered from I-90 and hardcoded to USCIS conventions (Part. A. 1. tooltips, Part A-G, ~70 USCIS field names). Generalizing it via more regexes (or field-name parsing) is a heuristic treadmill -- and the data proves no single signal is reliable: I-90 encodes structure in field NAMES (P1_Line3a_FamilyName), I-589 names are OPAQUE (CheckBox31, TextField1[8], 0 dotted paths). So: KEEP acroform_dump.py as a generic exact-token oracle, RETIRE the USCIS heuristic layer, and move ALL structural reasoning onto a strong LLM fed a deliberately-assembled bundle of EVERY structural signal the PDF exposes (widget names+flags+rects+tooltips+choices ALREADY captured; ADD dotted XFA path, name-token decomposition, tab order, spatial clusters, rendered page). Division of labor: deterministic = exact tokens (anti-hallucination anchor); LLM = meaning + relationships + naming convention (via contract rule + few-shot from the I-90 gold standard).

KNOWN (verified): acroform_dump.py is fully generic; the LLM already reasons structure well and only MIS-NAMES section_id (0% vs 88.3%) -- a convention mismatch, not a capability gap, fixable with few-shot; field-name structure varies wildly form-to-form (the central finding); no automated Claude extractor exists yet (overlaps 7a9.8).

OPEN QUESTIONS to explore (detail in proposal): Q1 can few-shot make the LLM match section_id convention (retires the deterministic section-id layer)? Q2 what structural signal does the in-repo non-USCIS W-7 actually expose (do this 10-min probe FIRST)? Q3 which enrichment signals help vs noise (ablation)? Q4 will the LLM faithfully COPY exact widget names or hallucinate (anti-hallucination; may need name-reference+rehydrate)? Q5 table/multi-entry consolidation from the bundle? Q6 model/cost/context-budget shape (big-form chunking)? Q7 where (if anywhere) does the deterministic pass still beat the LLM?

DELIVERABLES: W-7 probe; a generic structural-enrichment pass on acroform_dump; an LLM (b)-pass harness (pluggable model; coordinate with 7a9.8); scored vs existing arms on I-90+I-589 (7a9.3 scorer) + qualitative read on W-7; answers to Q1-Q7; recommendation on retiring the deterministic intelligence layer.

INTEGRATION (maintainer-agreed): when built, ADD IT AS A NEW ARM to the bake-off (manifest.json + harness) for head-to-head scoring. Relates to 7a9.8 (de-risks its architecture) but is its own exploration; do NOT touch the live app.

title: Build the fused authoring pipeline (deterministic skeleton -> strong-LLM (b) pass)
description:
Promote the throwaway scripts/bakeoff/ arms into a real PDF->JSON authoring tool, per the 7a9.5 recommendation. Pipeline: PyMuPDF deterministic pass (old-extractor heuristic + tooltip-hierarchy parse) emits the schema skeleton -- EXACT widget names, types, flags, /TU tooltips, rects (pdf_position), schema-conformant section_ids/ordering -- then feeds skeleton + PDF to a strong LLM for the (b) reasoning pass (consolidate widget groups, synthesize show_if/controls_fields/copy_to/overflow from printed conditional text, detect tables). Output: draft schema.json for human correction in the schema-editor (7a9.6).

Engine: Claude Opus 4.8 (claude-hybrid) default -- it led I-90 conditionals AND won I-589 tables (7/9), and the residual hours are table/multi-entry-heavy. Keep --model pluggable so gemini-3.5-flash-hybrid is a cheaper/faster swap (it edges I-589 conditional recall and completes the heavy I-589 call gemini-3.1-pro times out on). NO Document AI (dropped 2026-06-06, maintainer; AcroForm dump supersedes its (a) layer, nothing for (b)).

Acceptance: a runnable, --model-pluggable authoring pipeline that takes a form.pdf and emits a draft FormSchema (docs/schema_format.md / backend/models/form_models.py shape), reusing the validated bakeoff arms; scored no worse than the best bakeoff hybrid on the 7a9.3 harness for both I-90 and I-589.
notes: ENGINE COST/WIRING (maintainer steer, 2026-06-07): the (b) engine default is the Claude SUBAGENT path (Claude Code Agent tool on the maintainer's subscription), NOT the Anthropic API. The bake-off's claude-hybrid arms were produced this way -- there is deliberately NO arm_claude.py / anthropic SDK / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in scripts/bakeoff/ (the drafts are pre-computed JSON the scorer reads). Build 7a9.8 on the SAME subagent path: it is effectively free on the subscription, whereas a Gemini call goes through arm_gemini.py (google-genai SDK) and is METERED per-token. So claude-via-subagent is the CHEAPER default for this maintainer, and gemini-3.5-flash-hybrid is the paid/alternate swap (reverse of the usual 'API = cheap' intuition). Do NOT wire an Anthropic API key unless the pipeline must run headless/unattended where no Claude Code subagent is available -- that would be a new paid dependency to escalate.

title: Spacebar PTT: held-key repeat floods console; first-press PTT may not engage

The repeat-guard (if (!e.repeat && isConnected) handlePushToTalkPress()) is correct in intent -- OS key-repeat SHOULD be ignored -- so the repeat spam itself is expected, but: (a) it is noisy console spam worth throttling/removing now that PTT is past bring-up, and (b) the user reports the PTT does NOT engage on press ('instead of clicking the PTT, I get the following'), suggesting the FIRST (non-repeat) keydown's handlePushToTalkPress() is a no-op or the keyup/press cycle isn't starting capture. The pasted log starts mid-hold (all repeat:true), so the first event isn't shown -- reproduce and capture the first keydown to confirm whether handlePushToTalkPress fires and whether AudioManager starts capturing. title: Prevent telemetry git collisions: union-merge ledger + derive counter from ledger
description:
PROBLEM: every /closeout appends a row to docs/journal/harness_ledger.jsonl AND rewrites .beads/experiment_state.json, committing both to the feature branch. Parallel PRs collide on dev: (1) ledger = trivial keep-both line conflict every time (e.g. PR #75 vs #76); (2) experiment_state.json = whole-file counter rewrite -> SILENT undercount when two same-arm sessions both bump baseline_A (a correctness bug).

FIX (user-approved, two parts):
1. Union-merge the ledger: add checked-in .gitattributes with 'docs/journal/harness_ledger.jsonl merge=union' (union is a git BUILT-IN driver, no .git/config registration, verified on git 2.53). Append conflicts then auto-keep-both, no manual resolution ever.
2. Make the counter DERIVABLE from the ledger so it can't lose increments: replace bump_experiment_state's read-mutate-write with derive_experiment_state(ledger_path) that counts rows by 'arm' field (baseline_A = #arm=='A', etc.). title: [bug] closeout_finish.py writes telemetry AFTER its commit+push, orphaning the last ledger row
description:
ROOT CAUSE: in scripts/closeout_finish.py steps() (the open-PR plan), the ordered steps are: commit (already-staged closeout work) -> rebase -> push -> open PR -> [request review] -> telemetry. The 'telemetry' step (self.telemetry, which runs harness_ledger.py) APPENDS the ledger row to docs/journal/harness_ledger.jsonl and bumps .beads/experiment_state.json AFTER the only commit and AFTER the push. No step git-adds/commits/pushes those two files. So every closeout leaves its OWN telemetry row uncommitted in the working tree.

WHY IT LOOKED OK: historically the row was captured out-of-band -- either a human made a dedicated 'chore(harness): PR #NN telemetry row' commit afterward (see commits b92e1fa/f349670/8f9d071/d3b2388), or it got swept accidentally into the orchestrator's NEXT fix commit (e.g. PR #64's row rode along in 7310e50). When nothing follows the closeout (a --skip-review PR with no further commits, or the last run on a branch), the row is orphaned and lost if the worktree is archived/discarded. Maintainer hit this: 'M .beads/experiment_state.json / M docs/journal/harness_ledger.jsonl' dirty at archive time = real telemetry the tool wrote but never persisted. (Rescued the P#67/4ok row by hand in commit 1f0400b.)

SCOPE: affects BOTH the open-PR path (telemetry written post-push) and any run where the row is the last write. The --close-only path correctly writes NO row (hrn.15), so it's not implicated. experiment_state.json (arm counter) has the same orphaning.

FIX (recommended, option A): make the telemetry step commit+push its OWN two files (git add docs/journal/harness_ledger.jsonl .beads/experiment_state.json && git commit -m 'chore(harness): PR #NN telemetry row' && push). This does NOT violate the script's 'never git add the orchestrator's content' rule -- telemetry is the TOOL's own bookkeeping, not reviewable PR content. (Option B -- write the row BEFORE the commit step so it rides the closeout commit -- was rejected: it dumps telemetry noise into the reviewed PR diff.) Note the post-push ordering means the telemetry commit lands after the PR's push, so the step must push again (or telemetry must move before push). Acceptance: after a closeout (both review-worthy and --skip-review), the working tree is CLEAN -- no orphaned ledger/experiment_state changes; the row is committed and on the pushed branch. Add a dry-run plan line for the telemetry commit/push.

title: Investigate: make closeout cheaper — script the deterministic glue + delegate mechanical closeout to a Haiku subagent
description:
PROBLEM (observed on hrn.12 closeout): a single-file doctrine reword took ~25 orchestrator turns end-to-end and ~9+ just for the /closeout ceremony, almost all on the most expensive public model. Turn audit: ~half were pure mechanics with ZERO judgment (journal scaffold read-before-write dance = 3 turns alone; stash/branch/pop/verify = 4; commit/push/rebase/file-bead/mark-in-progress = 5); ~quarter were light summarization a cheap model handles (journal prose, doc-freshness triage, the touches-only-.md review-worthiness gate); only ~15-20% was real judgment (diagnosis, the actual edits, fresh-eyes triage). Opus tokens spent on git plumbing.

PROPOSAL (two layers, not either/or):
1. SCRIPT the deterministic glue. closeout_prep/journal_scaffold/closeout_housekeeping exist but the GLUE is hand-driven turn-by-turn. A closeout_finish.py that, given a bead id + filled journal body, does branch/stash/commit/push/file-bead/open-PR/telemetry in ONE call collapses ~10 turns into 1. Fix the journal-scaffold own-goal: accept prose as an arg (or print path+template) so there is no Write-fails-Read-Write dance. The script layer should ENCAPSULATE the SKILL scar-tissue traps (WT-vs-R worktree path resolution, pr_review_watcher --since discipline, read-before-write) so neither a cheap model nor the orchestrator re-navigates them.
2. DELEGATE the mechanical closeout to a HAIKU subagent. Once the orchestrator DECIDES this-bead-is-done-here-is-the-diff, the rest is a bounded procedure fully written in the 372-line SKILL — ideal for a cheaper model (the SKILL is the prompt). Orchestrator keeps judgment (what to build, the edits, fresh-eyes adopt/reject, ambiguous review-worthiness, escalation); hands script-glue + journal-from-brief + telemetry to Haiku, which reports back.

DIVIDING LINE: anything that CHANGES WHAT SHIPS stays with the orchestrator; everything downstream of this-is-ready is delegable.

CAUTION: the SKILL carries hard-won scar tissue (worktree path traps, --since timestamps, read-before-write). A Haiku subagent on the raw SKILL is MORE likely to trip these than Opus, so SCRIPT-FIRST is the safer order — encapsulate traps in the script, THEN delegate. Delegating without scripting first trades token cost for error rate.

OPEN QUESTIONS for review: (a) fold into the A/B arm framework (a new arm-D = delegated closeout, measured on the ledger)? (b) one big closeout_finish.py vs several small composable scripts? (c) which exact steps cross the judgment line (review-worthiness gate: scriptable, or keep with orchestrator when ambiguous)? (d) the hard rule that beads writes are orchestrator/main-thread only — a Haiku subagent cannot do bd writes, so those stay with the orchestrator or go through the script. This bead is for REVIEW/design, not immediate implementation.

title: Live API 1007: VAD config sends disabled:true AND sensitivity fields together (rejected) — on dev AND main
description:
DISCOVERED 2026-05-31 while running the tak token-cost spike against the real Live API. The adapter's VAD config builder (backend/adapters/live_ai_gemini.py ~625-645) sets automatic_activity_detection.disabled=True (when DISABLE_GEMINI_VAD=True, the DEFAULT) and THEN unconditionally also adds start_of_speech_sensitivity / end_of_speech_sensitivity / prefix_padding_ms / silence_duration_ms from the VAD_* settings. The Live API now REJECTS that combination on connect with:

  1007 (invalid frame payload data) 'automatic_activity_detection.disabled is true, but the following fields were also set: start_of_speech_sensitivity, end_of_speech_sensitivity...'

Reproduced with both gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview and (by the same code path) the 2.5 native model, using the DEFAULT config (DISABLE_GEMINI_VAD=True, VAD_START/END_SENSITIVITY=LOW, VAD_PREFIX_PADDING_MS=500, VAD_SILENCE_DURATION_MS=500). The session fails to connect -> no turns.

SEVERITY: potentially a live connect-failure on the default config. The block exists on origin/main (prod) too (verified via git show origin/main), not just dev — so this is NOT introduced by recent work; the API appears to have tightened enforcement (or the deployed demo image predates these VAD_* fields). bd daa noted the demo 'works' as of 2026-05-30, so either the demo runs an older image or enforcement is very recent — NEEDS confirmation against the actual demo deploy.

FIX (proposed): when disabled=True, send ONLY {disabled: True} — do not add any sensitivity/padding fields. I.e. gate the VAD_* additions behind 'not DISABLE_GEMINI_VAD'. Conversely the sensitivity/padding fields apply only when automatic detection is ENABLED.

INTERSECTS: bd polyglot-pdf-333 (native-VAD smoke test toggles DISABLE_GEMINI_VAD=False — that path sends the sensitivity fields, which is correct there) and bd polyglot-pdf-daa (1011 investigation). Confirm whether this 1007 is currently hitting the live demo before deciding urgency.

So the frontend must gate the manual signals on the same toggle (don't send them in native mode), and the client must send continuous audio (not VAD-gated/suppressed) so Gemini's VAD has a stream to detect on. Audit audioManager.ts (skips silent chunks at ~:214) — native VAD likely needs the silence too.
3. Keep DISABLE_GEMINI_VAD as the single toggle (or add a clearer NATIVE_VAD flag) that switches BOTH backend config AND frontend manual-signal/audio-gating behavior together, so we can revert to manual VAD in one switch if the native VAD is still bad. Document it.
4. Validate both modes work: native-VAD mode functional, and flipping back to manual VAD restores current behavior.

Related: DISABLE_GEMINI_VAD is documented in docs/standards/voice-and-vad.md (bead 4rz, planned). See docs/genai_docs/ for SDK syntax on realtime_input_config / activity signals.

title: Retire manual disconnect/restart/carry-over context hacks made redundant by compression
description: Phase 4 of epic l3a. Coordinate with bd polyglot-pdf-umv (restart loses section metadata) — some of that may become moot. Idle-timeout watchdog (WS_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SEC) just CLOSES the WS on inactivity (health/UX, no finalize call); Level-3 finalize is a FRONTEND-initiated farewell (UX); section-switch restart is an intentional reset. Context grows unbounded today. So there is NOTHING to retire -- scope shrinks to a verification/cleanup pass (confirm no restart path implicitly bounded cost; coordinate w/ umv). Epic title 'replace manual disconnect/restart hacks' predates this audit. Gate compression behind CONTEXT_COMPRESSION_ENABLED for one-env-var revert.

The nv0 design audit had ALREADY shrunk 7kp to near-nothing (there was no cost-motivated context-bounding hack to retire -- the idle-timeout watchdog, farewell finalize, and section-switch restart are all UX/lifecycle mechanisms that stay). With compression dead, there is nothing for 7kp to do. The restart-loses-section-metadata concern it referenced lives independently in bd umv. Closing per maintainer (clear moot compression beads).

title: copilot_watch.py crashes on UnicodeEncodeError when printing verdict detail (cp1252 stdout)
description: copilot_watch.py sets encoding='utf-8', errors='replace' on its subprocess READ of the GitHub API (line ~154) but NOT on its own stdout. When _emit()/print(detail) runs on Windows (default cp1252 stdout) and the detail contains a non-cp1252 char (e.g. U+2192 '->' arrow quoted from a PR body/Copilot comment), print() raises UnicodeEncodeError and the watcher crashes with exit 1 -- masquerading as an ERROR verdict even though Copilot actually completed (the crash happened in _emit('COMMENTS', ...), AND again in the ERROR fallback _emit). Hit live during closeout of bd polyglot-pdf-4ln on PR #27. Fix: reconfigure sys.stdout/sys.stderr to utf-8 errors='replace' at module load (guarded for detached streams), same pattern bd polyglot-pdf-4ln added to scripts/bd_prime.py. This is the same UTF-8 bug class as bd polyglot-pdf-39a but on the OUTPUT side.
close_reason: Already fixed: copilot_watch.py output path is UTF-8-safe via _setup_utf8_stdio() (main() first line) + _emit->_safe_print UnicodeEncodeError fallback (landed bd 39a + PR #24 guard restore). Empirically reproduced amy's exact scenario (U+2192 + emoji on cp1252 stdout) -> no crash, both layers hold. No code change.

comments.author: caellwynai-josh
comments.text:
VERIFIED ALREADY FIXED (2026-05-31). The output-side UTF-8 crash amy describes is covered by the current code: scripts/copilot_watch.py has _setup_utf8_stdio() (reconfigures stdout/stderr to utf-8, errors='replace') called as the FIRST line of main():618, AND _emit()->_safe_print() wraps print() in a UnicodeEncodeError fallback that re-encodes with errors='replace'. This is the same fix class amy asked for. Landed via bd 39a (commits 71480b3/7da386b) + the PR #24 'restore reverted UTF-8 guard' (2f89713) — the guard had been reverted, which is likely why the 4ln/PR#27 crash that prompted amy still happened on the pre-restore version.

REPRODUCTION TEST (both layers hold): simulated a strict cp1252 stdout, then called _emit('COMMENTS', detail) with detail containing U+2192 '->' arrow + 💡 emoji (the exact chars amy names): returns 0, no crash. Also confirmed _safe_print's fallback alone (without _setup_utf8_stdio) survives the same input. No code change needed.

title: restart_gemini_session passes 4 non-existent callback methods -> AttributeError on every WS restart
description:
FormFillingService.restart_gemini_session (backend/services/form_filling_service.py:385-389) calls self._live_ai.set_callbacks() with on_form_update=self.handle_form_update, on_transcript=self.handle_transcript, on_audio=self.handle_audio, on_tool_call=self.handle_tool_call -- but NONE of handle_form_update / handle_transcript / handle_audio / handle_tool_call are defined on FormFillingService (grep `def handle_*` => empty). So set_callbacks raises AttributeError as soon as the method body reaches that line.

REACHABILITY / impact: reachable in prod. websocket_routes.py:463 calls `await service.restart_gemini_session(next_field_hint=...)` on a client "restart_gemini_session" message (websocket_routes.py:454). It is wrapped in try/except that logs restart_gemini_session_failed (websocket_routes.py:467) -- so the restart SILENTLY FAILS rather than crashing the socket. Any feature relying on mid-session Gemini restart (e.g. section switch / language change that triggers a restart) is broken on this path.

CONTRAST with the working path: the other set_callbacks call sites at form_filling_service.py:156 and :169 pass DIFFERENT, presumably-correct callbacks (the on_* handlers used at session create). restart_gemini_session looks like it was written against a stale handler-naming scheme (handle_* vs the real names) and never ran -- consistent with the e9v finding that this file could not be imported, so this code path was never exercised by tests either.

DO: find the real handler methods/callbacks used by the working set_callbacks calls (form_filling_service.py:156/169) and make restart_gemini_session pass those same (correct) callables. Then add/repair a unit test that actually invokes restart_gemini_session with a mocked live_ai and asserts set_callbacks is called with valid callables (this would have caught it; ties into the test-revival work in polyglot-pdf-0rx).

title: In-house staging->prod deploy gate: clone staging in same GCP project + Deploy-to-Staging/Prod skills with digest-promotion guard
description:
DECISION (2026-05-30): Keep the SPIRIT of the review->stage->prod flow but drop the GitHub deploy gate (it can't see manual Firebase/Cloud Run deploys; required_deployments was inert). Enforce the staging gate IN-HOUSE instead. Architecture frozen: classic Firebase Hosting + Cloud Run (see [[architecture-decision-2026-05-30-final-keep-classic]]).

ENV MODEL (per owner): ONE GCP/Firebase project (polyglot-demo-aa709) holds BOTH envs -- required for billing consolidation, IAM, service accounts. Within it:
- PROD (current 'demo' role becomes prod): Cloud Run 'polyglot-backend' + prod frontend hosting target. This is the investor/pilot-facing env (app is NOT in paid production yet).
- STAGING (new, cloned once from prod): a second Cloud Run service (e.g. 'polyglot-backend-staging') + a second Firebase Hosting target/site in the same project. GCP confirmed supports 2 backends + 2 frontend routes in one project.
- Retire/ignore the GCP-blocked polyglot-forms-919f2.

TWO SKILLS:
- 'Deploy to Staging': build image, deploy to staging Cloud Run service + staging hosting target. CAPTURE the resulting immutable image DIGEST (gcloud run services describe <staging> --format='value(spec.template.spec.containers[0].image)' returns @sha256:...).
- 'Deploy to Prod': GATE = (1) health-check staging /health returns 200 (endpoint exists, added in 9dq); (2) ensure the artifact going to prod is the SAME as what's verified on staging by reading staging's live image digest and deploying THAT DIGEST to prod (gcloud run deploy <prod> --image <staging-digest>) rather than rebuilding -- structurally prevents shipping an untested artifact; (3) promote the same frontend build/version. Human smoke-test of staging stays in the loop; the digest+health checks are machine-enforced and un-skippable.

CURRENT-STATE GAP to fix: deploy-all.sh builds with a FLOATING tag (gcr.io//polyglot-backend, no digest) and rebuilds per env. The new flow must pin and promote by DIGEST so staging==prod is verifiable, not 'same git commit' (which can rebuild differently).

OPEN: owner installed firebase tools/skills this session -- check whether any (e.g. a firebase deploy skill or hosting-targets tooling) simplifies the multi-site frontend split before hand-rolling. Also: how to wire two frontend Hosting targets in firebase.json (firebase target:apply hosting <name> <site>) + the /api/** rewrite per target pointing at the right Cloud Run service.

GitHub side stays as-is: To Dev ruleset (PR + Copilot review) is the external-review gate; unit tests run LOCALLY (owner: ~1 bug to prod since adopting review; not forcing Copilot to re-run regression). main ruleset's inert required_deployments gate should be dropped or repointed -- tracked as the remaining loose end.

Refs: deploy-all.sh:120-134 (build+deploy), backend/main.py /health . bd memory [deploy-model-confirmed...], [architecture-decision-2026-05-30-final...].
acceptance_criteria: Staging is a --no-traffic --tag staging revision of the single polyglot-backend Cloud Run service (+ a staging Firebase hosting target); 'Deploy to Staging' and 'Deploy to Prod' skills exist; Deploy-to-Prod refuses unless the staging tag revision /health is green, then promotes THAT SAME revision to 100% traffic (no rebuild) via update-traffic; WebSocket behavior during traffic switch is verified or promotion is documented as between-calls-only; frontend promoted in lockstep; docs/doctrine describe the in-house revision-promotion gate.
notes:
DESIGN COMPLETE -- ready to build (2026-05-30). This bead is now fully specced across the notes above; no open design questions block starting. NEXT AGENT START HERE:

RECOMMENDED FIRST STEP = a SPIKE, not the full build. Before writing the deploy skills, verify the two unknowns that the whole design leans on, against a throwaway --no-traffic --tag staging revision of the real polyglot-backend service:
  1. WebSocket connectivity AT the tag URL (https://staging---polyglot-backend-<hash>.a.run.app) -- does a Gemini Live voice session work end-to-end through it?
  2. WS reconnect behavior across an update-traffic flip -- does an active call ride out on the old revision, and does the existing reconnect flow re-establish cleanly on the new one?
The spike result confirms (or redirects) the cutover-window choice. Hypothesis already favored: Option 1 (tight sequential flip: update-traffic then hosting:clone) + a 'reconnecting' toast is sufficient, because session state survives in sessionStorage w/ migrations (verified) and reconnect is already handled. Backward-compat WS contracts (Option b) is a LATER upgrade for paid-prod, not a prerequisite.

BUILD ORDER after the spike: (a) stand up staging Firebase hosting target/site with /api/** -> tag URL (verify channel-vs-site supports per-target rewrites); (b) 'Deploy to Staging' skill (build, deploy --no-traffic --tag staging, print tag URL); (c) 'Deploy to Prod' skill (gate: staging /health 200 -> update-traffic --to-tags staging=100 -> firebase hosting:clone staging->live); (d) docs/doctrine update; (e) drop/repoint main's inert required_deployments gate (see loose-end below). Keep writing schemaFormState.ts migrations on any state-shape change.

All mechanics, commands, caveats, and the session-state analysis are in the preceding notes. Refs in-bead.

title: Evaluate Firebase App Hosting (native GitHub Checks + staging/prod envs) to realize the review->stage->prod flow
description:
GOAL: capture the SPIRIT of the branch-protection flow -- internal unit tests, internal review, external (Copilot) review, green staged preview, THEN prod -- in the most streamlined native way, rather than hand-rolling GitHub Deployment-object plumbing on classic Hosting (the approach in superseded bead 9qt).

RESEARCH (2026-05-30, firebase.google.com/docs/app-hosting/*):
- App Hosting natively integrates with the GitHub CHECKS API: each rollout posts a build/deploy status check into the PR. The right GitHub primitive for our gate is required_status_checks (wait for a named check to go green), NOT required_deployments -- much cleaner, no custom deployment objects.
- Native multi-environment: each environment = its own Firebase project + App Hosting backend, with a designated live branch (dev->staging project, main->prod project) and apphosting.<env>.yaml config overrides. Branch->environment is first-class.
- Runs on Cloud Run underneath; builds the repo via Cloud Build (buildpacks) on git push to the live branch. Automatic or manual rollouts.

KEY RISKS / OPEN QUESTIONS (these decide go/no-go):
1. BACKEND FIT (linchpin): App Hosting targets WEB FRAMEWORKS (Next.js/Angular, or anything emitting their web-bundle spec). Our backend is a PYTHON/FastAPI WEBSOCKET app, currently a separate Cloud Run service behind firebase.json's /api/** rewrite. Google does NOT document Python backend support, and App Hosting is 'one web app per backend', not 'static frontend + separate WS service'. MUST verify whether a FastAPI/WebSocket backend can run on App Hosting at all, or whether only the FRONTEND moves to App Hosting while the backend stays Cloud Run / moves to Railway.
2. RAILWAY INTERACTION: a possible backend move to Railway (voice-model latency, same intranet) conflicts with App Hosting also putting the backend on Cloud Run. Likely outcome: frontend on App Hosting (native Checks flow), backend on Railway or Cloud Run -- App Hosting then owns only the frontend half of the flow. Decide the topology before migrating.
3. PROJECTS: would need a staging Firebase project distinct from demo(polyglot-demo-aa709)/prod(polyglot-forms-919f2). Map which is which.
4. WebSocket support on App Hosting's Cloud Run + CDN/LB path (long-lived connections) needs confirming.

DELIVERABLE: a go/no-go recommendation with the chosen topology (App Hosting vs classic Hosting+CloudRun vs Railway-backend), and which gates live in GitHub (unit-test status check + Copilot review on dev PRs -- Copilot gate stays as-is per owner) vs Firebase (staging rollout check). If GO, this supersedes 9qt and spawns the implementation beads.

Refs: firebase.google.com/docs/app-hosting/about-app-hosting , /multiple-environments , /rollouts ; docs.github.com required_status_checks. See bd memory [deploy-model-confirmed-2026-05-30...].
acceptance_criteria: Documented go/no-go on App Hosting with a concrete topology decision (frontend + backend placement) and the resulting gate stack (which gates in GitHub vs Firebase); the FastAPI/WebSocket-backend-on-App-Hosting question is definitively answered; if GO, 9qt is superseded and implementation beads are filed.
notes:
COST MODELING (must be part of the go/no-go, researched 2026-05-30):

The decisive cost fact for THIS app: a Cloud Run instance with ANY open WebSocket is billed ACTIVE for the whole connection lifetime (instance-based billing, ~$0.000018/vCPU-sec ≈ $0.065/vCPU-hr). So the 'serverless scales to zero' win only applies BETWEEN calls, not during them. App Hosting runs on Cloud Run, so it inherits this exact model.

Cost comparison axes to quantify (build a small model, don't hand-wave):
- Cloud Run / App Hosting: instance-based billing during calls + $0 when idle (true scale-to-zero between sessions). Cost ≈ (concurrent-call-minutes) × (vCPU+mem rate) + egress (audio out is the big egress line -- 24kHz PCM). Cheapest for BURSTY/intermittent demo traffic.
- Railway: always-on. $0.028/vCPU-hr + $0.014/GB-hr RAM + $0.10/GB egress + $0.25/GB storage. Pays even when idle (~$10/mo for an idle container). Cheaper per-hour but no scale-to-zero. Typical real apps $20-50/mo.
- TENSION TO RESOLVE: Railway's pull is LATENCY (same intranet as the voice model). But for intermittent voice sessions, Cloud Run's scale-to-zero is likely CHEAPER. So latency-vs-idle-cost is the actual trade-off the model must price. Also weigh: audio egress ($/GB) differs by provider and is non-trivial for 24kHz audio_out; and the Gemini Live token cost (now family-keyed, polyglot-pdf-lky) dwarfs hosting cost per session -- so hosting choice may be latency-driven, not cost-driven, once modeled. CONFIRM that.

DELIVERABLE addition: a back-of-envelope cost model per topology at a few traffic levels (e.g. 10 / 100 / 1000 call-minutes per day), including audio egress, alongside the latency and the WebSocket-support findings. The recommendation should state whether the topology choice is cost-driven or latency-driven (hypothesis: latency-driven, because Gemini token cost >> hosting cost per call).

Refs: cloud.google.com/run/pricing + run/docs/triggering/websockets ; railway.com/pricing .
close_reason: DECISION (2026-05-30): NO-GO on App Hosting / Railway. Keep current architecture: classic Firebase Hosting (frontend) + Cloud Run (Python/FastAPI WebSocket backend). Rationale: (1) Cloud Run is co-located with Gemini (both Google products, same network) -> LOWEST latency AND, with scale-to-zero between calls, cheapest for bursty voice traffic; Railway loses on BOTH latency and idle cost. (2) App Hosting targets web frameworks (Next/Angular), not a separate Python/WebSocket backend -- wrong product. (3) Per-session Gemini token cost >> hosting cost, so hosting is not the cost lever anyway. Architecture stays as-is; no migration. Remaining CI question (how the GitHub flow gates without a native deploy feeder) tracked separately.

title: Wire Firebase preview-channel deploys as the 'staging' gate for the main ruleset (GitHub Actions)
description:
CONTEXT: Deploys are currently LOCAL + manual (deploy-demo.sh / deploy-production.sh run gcloud Cloud Run + firebase hosting against polyglot-demo-aa709 / polyglot-forms-919f2; firebase CLI is installed; gated on caellwyn@gmail.com gcloud account). The 'Defend Production' ruleset on main has a required_deployments->staging rule that NOTHING currently satisfies (no GitHub-driven deploy), so it would block every dev->main promotion. This bead makes that gate real via Firebase Hosting preview channels.

DESIGN (decided 2026-05-30):
- PR into dev -> GitHub Actions deploys frontend to a Firebase PREVIEW CHANNEL (one per PR, unique URL, ~7-day expiry) via FirebaseExtended/action-hosting-deploy, AND creates a GitHub Deployment object against the 'staging' environment reporting success. This is what satisfies a staging gate.
- Merge to main -> deploy to the Firebase LIVE channel (prod) and report a 'production' deployment.
- KEY GAP: action-hosting-deploy by default only comments a preview URL on the PR; it does NOT create a GitHub Deployment against an environment. The workflow must explicitly create the deployment (actions/github-script or bobheadxi/deployments) so the ruleset's required_deployments rule sees green.

OPEN QUESTIONS / SUBTASKS:
- Firebase CI service account: run 'firebase init hosting:github' to scaffold the workflow + upload the encrypted SA key as a GitHub secret (FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_*). Confirm which project (demo vs prod) maps to staging vs prod.
- Backend: preview channels are FRONTEND/Hosting only. The /api/** rewrite points at Cloud Run (polyglot-backend, us-central1). Decide whether 'staging' deploys a separate Cloud Run revision/service or the preview frontend just points at the existing backend. (Ties into the possible Railway move.)
- The required_deployments rule currently targets main; preview=staging. Confirm whether to ALSO add a staging gate on dev, or keep dev gated only by PR+Copilot and main gated by the production deploy.
- Until this lands, the main deploy gate is inert and main is intentionally un-mergeable (all work targets dev) -- acceptable per owner.

Refs: firebase.google.com/docs/hosting/github-integration ; github.com/FirebaseExtended/action-hosting-deploy ; docs.github.com/actions/.../deployments-and-environments . See docs/doctrine/branch-protection-setup.md for the current ruleset definitions.
acceptance_criteria: A GitHub Actions workflow deploys dev PRs to a Firebase preview channel and reports a successful 'staging' deployment that satisfies the 'Defend Production' ruleset; merging to main deploys to the live channel and reports 'production'; docs/doctrine/branch-protection-setup.md + promotion-tiers.md updated to describe the real (Firebase, not GitHub-generic) pipeline.

title: copilot_watch.py crashes on Windows (cp1252) when Copilot comment contains emoji/non-latin1
description: scripts/copilot_watch.py prints Copilot's review detail via print(detail); on Windows the default stdout encoding is cp1252, so a Copilot comment containing an emoji (observed: U+1F4A1 light-bulb) raises UnicodeEncodeError and crashes the watcher AFTER it already classified the review as COMMENTS. The watcher then misreports ERROR. Fix: force UTF-8 stdout (e.g. sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')) or encode-safe the print in _emit(). Found exercising the new dev PR flow on PR #12.

title: fix(voice): handleDisclaimerAgree falls through to switchToFirstSection after a SILENT reconnect timeout
description:
Pre-existing hazard in handleDisclaimerAgree, present on dev in BOTH VoiceOverlay.tsx and VoiceOverlayMobile.tsx. Surfaced by fresh-eyes during review of PR for bd ala0 (which fixed the unmatched-activity_end on the reconnect path and did NOT touch this); pre-existing, not introduced there.

THE HAZARD: on the stale-connection branch, handleDisclaimerAgree does 'await handleConnect()'. handleConnect() does NOT throw on a connection TIMEOUT -- it polls getStatus() for up to 5000ms, and on timeout it calls setError(...) and RETURNS NORMALLY (no throw). So after a silent timeout, control falls through to 'if (connectionManager && selectedLanguage) { ... await switchToFirstSection() }', which calls startSection() on a manager whose WS never came up -> 'Connection not initialized' throws, an unhandled rejection in handleDisclaimerAgree (there is no try/catch around steps 3-5). The user is left on a broken state with only the setError message.

NOTE: ala0's fix (skip sendActivityEnd on reconnect) made this path marginally SAFER (no spurious activity_end on a dead WS), but did not address the fall-through. The real fix: after handleConnect() on the reconnect branch, re-check connection status (or have handleConnect signal success/failure) and BAIL OUT (return after setError) instead of proceeding to switchToFirstSection when the reconnect did not actually connect. Apply to BOTH overlays. Confidence: medium (only bites when a reconnect TIMES OUT mid-disclaimer, a rare edge). Source: fresh-eyes on the ala0 PR.

title: fix(frontend): typeless WebSocket message sent at connection setup is silently dropped
description:

The guard is at frontend/src/webFormConnection.ts:1471 (in the WS send path). It fires once at connect time, BEFORE any user interaction (before disclaimer-agree), so some code path calls connection.send(obj) with an object that has no 'type' field. The backend inbound dispatch (websocket_routes.py) keys on message type, so a typeless message is dropped/ignored.

INVESTIGATE: trace which caller sends the typeless message at connection setup -- grep callers of the send method, walk the connect/handshake sequence in webFormConnection.ts. Determine whether it is a real dropped message (something the backend should have received) or a harmless dead send. Then either fix the caller to include a 'type' or remove the dead send.

title: fix(voice): disclaimer-agree reconnect path sends unmatched activity_end (both overlays)
description:
Pre-existing logic hazard in handleDisclaimerAgree, present on dev in BOTH VoiceOverlay.tsx and VoiceOverlayMobile.tsx (identical structure). Surfaced by fresh-eyes on PR #146 (zq9l), which only ADDED the top-of-handler interrupt and did NOT touch this block -- so the hazard is pre-existing, not introduced by that PR.

THE HAZARD: handleDisclaimerAgree sends sendActivityStart() near the top (now in both overlays after zq9l). Then it checks isConnectionActive; if the connection went stale during the long disclaimer read, it calls handleConnect() to build a BRAND-NEW connection. It then unconditionally falls through to 'if (connectionManager && selectedLanguage) { ...; await sendActivityEnd(); switchToFirstSection(); }'. On the reconnect path, the new connection never received a sendActivityStart from this handler (the start went to the OLD/stale connection, or no-oped if the WS wasn't open) -- so sendActivityEnd is sent against a fresh session with no open user turn: an unmatched/orphaned activity_end. In native VAD the backend converts activity_end -> audio_stream_end, which on a turn that never opened could confuse session state or log a spurious warning.

FIX (apply to BOTH overlays to keep them consistent): on the reconnect branch, either (a) re-send sendActivityStart after handleConnect() before the later sendActivityEnd, or (b) skip the sendActivityEnd when the reconnect path was taken (the fresh session's switchToFirstSection drives the turn). Decide which, mirror in both files, and verify in manual-VAD mode (native suppresses activity_start so the imbalance only bites manual). Confidence: medium (rare stale-connection edge case; backend may tolerate the unmatched end). Source: fresh-eyes on PR #146.
notes:
FIXED in both overlays (chose option b: skip activity_end on reconnect). In handleDisclaimerAgree (VoiceOverlay.tsx + VoiceOverlayMobile.tsx), added a 'reconnected' flag set true when the stale-connection branch calls handleConnect(); the later 'Step 4' sendActivityEnd() is now guarded by 'if (!reconnected)'. Rationale: on reconnect the earlier sendActivityStart opened the turn on the OLD/stale connection, so the fresh connection has no matching open turn -- activity_end there is unmatched (native VAD -> spurious audio_stream_end on a turn that never opened). switchToFirstSection restarts Gemini cleanly and drives the new turn, so the end is unnecessary. resumePlayback + switchToFirstSection still run on both paths; the NON-reconnect (common) path is unchanged.

Chose (b) over (a) re-send-activity_start-after-reconnect: the upcoming session RESTART (switchToFirstSection -> startSection) makes a turn-close on the soon-to-be-replaced session meaningless, so not sending it is the cleaner model.

Locked by 2 new tests in VoiceOverlay.disclaimer.test.tsx (desktop+mobile): force the connection stale post-mount via a __forceStale() mock hook, click Agree, assert connect() ran, switchToFirstSection ran, and sendActivityEnd was NOT called. Proven meaningful: git-stashing the source fix makes BOTH reconnect tests fail. Full FE suite 254 pass; added lines ASCII. Verification: deterministic unit tests judged sufficient (a browser repro needs a mid-disclaimer-read disconnect, which is flaky to force and adds nothing over the test that exercises the exact branch).

title: 0y7 unconfirmable loop-breaker is per-field -- no session-wide cap for cross-field confirm spin
description: Noticed during wpw.3 review (Codex flagged the same gap in the NEW validation-reject breaker, fixed there with a session-wide cap). The OLDER 0y7 unconfirmable-confirm loop-breaker in webFormConnection.handleConfirmFieldRequest is keyed ONLY per-field (lastUnconfirmableFieldId + per-field counters). If the model alternates confirm_field calls across DIFFERENT empty fields (A empty -> B empty -> A empty ...), each field switch resets the per-field counter, so the re-prompt cap never engages and it can re-prompt on every cycle -- the same cross-field spin wpw.3 closed for validation rejects. Fix: add a session-wide reprompt cap to the 0y7 breaker too (mirror VALIDATION_REJECT_SESSION_CAP in wpw.3: a counter not reset on field change, only on connect/section-switch/successful-confirm). Lower priority than wpw.3's was -- the confirm path is gated by mandatory read-back so the alternation is less likely, but the gap is real. See journal 2026-06-10-bd-wpw.3-client-side-ai-validation.md.

title: FE locked-field rejects use the dead dependency_error channel -- model never told
description: Discovered during wpw.3. webFormConnection.handleUpdateFormFields sends a 'dependency_error' WS message when an AI value targets a locked/hidden field, intending to inform Gemini. But the backend (websocket_routes.py inbound dispatch) has NO handler for 'dependency_error' -- it falls through to unknown_control_message_type + an 'error' reply, so the locked-field reason NEVER reaches the model. The model only learns the field didn't fill via the absence of a form_updated, with no corrective guidance. Fix: route the locked-field reason through completion_message -> send_prompt (the proven in-band channel the 0y7/wpw.3 loop-breakers use) instead of dependency_error, OR add a backend handler for dependency_error that forwards to send_prompt. PII-free: send the field spoken_name + reason category, never values. Mirror the wpw.3 applyAiValueWithValidation/handleAiValueRejected pattern. Epic wpw (WS-E family) or standalone.

title: fix(frontend): wire ConnectionCallbacks onStopCapture/onFormComplete + decide sendRecoveryPrompt caller (split from exs)
description:
Split from polyglot-pdf-exs. The dead-code nit (remove isFieldConfirmed) was done in a later cleanup PR; these two remain because they are larger / need a decision:

1. handleConfirmFieldRequest (webFormConnection.ts ~1099/1109) reads this.callbacks.onStopCapture and this.callbacks.onFormComplete, but neither is declared on the ConnectionCallbacks interface (lines 51-64), so both are always undefined at runtime (TS2339, part of the pre-existing 24-error baseline). Effect: audio-stop-before-section-switch and the form-complete notification silently never fire. Fix: add onStopCapture?: () => void and onFormComplete?: () => void to ConnectionCallbacks and wire them in connection.ts createConnectionManager. (Touches the TS error baseline -- coordinate with any typecheck-gating work.)

2. sendRecoveryPrompt is defined on WebFormConnection (~1429) and proxied through ConnectionManager (shared/connection.ts:36/548), but nothing INVOKES connectionManager.sendRecoveryPrompt() -- the activity-watchdog call chain is plumbed but inert. DECISION needed: wire the watchdog caller, or mark the path disabled-until-<recovery-prompt-backend-ready>. (Backend recovery_prompt was broken under zy3; check current state post-PR #132 which restored RECOVERY_PROMPT_LEVEL_*.)

Source: #111/#113 0y7 merge audit (via exs).
notes: Item 2 (sendRecoveryPrompt watchdog caller) RESOLVED BY DECISION (maintainer, 2026-06-10): do NOT wire the watchdog caller. The verbal recovery-prompt path stays WIRED-BUT-INERT as a possible future accessibility feature (blind/low-vision). The primary recovery UX instead becomes a connection-timeout modal -> session-restore flow, captured as the new epic polyglot-pdf-jf6w (investigation/scoping first). So item 2 needs no code change here. This bead now narrows to ITEM 1 ONLY: add onStopCapture?/onFormComplete? to the ConnectionCallbacks interface and wire them in connection.ts createConnectionManager (they're read in handleConfirmFieldRequest but undefined at runtime -- TS2339, part of the 24-error baseline).

title: chore(mobile): reconcile handleDisclaimerAgree sendActivityStart vs desktop (split from cd0)

title: investigate: section-last-field confirm fires a next-field-hint request that races the FE section-switch teardown -> HINT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT
description:
Deferred finding from PR #141 fresh-eyes (bd wpw.2). PRE-EXISTING (not introduced by wpw.2 -- verified against origin/dev: the old fire-and-forget confirm ALSO called request_next_field_hint after the send, and the FE ALSO called switchToSection right after confirming the last field). So this is a pre-existing, by-design interaction, deferred rather than blocking wpw.2.

Symptom: on the LAST field of a section, _handle_confirm_field_tool returns (recorded:true) then calls request_next_field_hint(); meanwhile the FE's handleConfirmFieldRequest detects the section complete and calls switchToSection(), which tears down the WS. The get_next_field_hint send may land on the closing socket -> coordinator returns HINT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT -> Gemini gets next_field_hint:null + the 'do NOT assume the form is complete' message, right as the section IS correctly auto-advancing. Low practical impact (the FE advances regardless, and the new section's first-field hint arrives via the section-switch flow), but Gemini may emit a redundant 'what's next' prompt at the boundary.

Investigate: should _handle_confirm_field_tool SKIP the next-field-hint request when the FE ack indicates a section boundary is imminent (e.g. the FE could include a section_complete flag in confirm_field_response)? Or should the FE defer switchToSection until after answering the hint? Measure first via the dev-log tool_callback_result at a section boundary before changing anything (don't assume the cause -- scar).

description:

(fresh-eyes) backend/services/callback_handler.py:_handle_confirm_field_tool calls 'await self._request_coordinator.request_next_field_hint()' WITHOUT the 'if self._request_coordinator:' guard that send_form_update (same file) has. description:

title: Binary-suppress log filter never runs on structlog records
description:
## Context
Found during fresh-eyes review of bd polyglot-pdf-0uu (PR #100). backend/utils/logging.py attaches _BinarySuppressFilter to the root logger + named noisy loggers (addFilter on LOGGERS, never on the StreamHandler). structlog uses LoggerFactory() and logs through its own loggers; those records reach root via HANDLER propagation, which does NOT run the originating-logger's filters. Proven: a 2595-char structlog INFO line passes through unfiltered and the filter's .filter() is never invoked for structlog records. So the binary/long-message suppression is effectively inert for all structlog (JSON) output -- the bulk of backend logs. Likely fix: attach the filter to the StreamHandler instead of (or in addition to) the loggers. Low priority -- binary dumps are rare and the PII binary-suppression was belt-and-suspenders.
acceptance_criteria: _BinarySuppressFilter actually filters structlog JSON output (binary frame dumps / >2000-char INFO lines are suppressed as intended), OR the dead filter is removed if no longer needed.
notes: Correction (Copilot review of PR #100): the filter is NOT categorically inert on structlog output. A logging.Filter runs on the EMITTING logger only. It IS attached to root + the noisy loggers, so structlog calls whose underlying stdlib logger is root or a noisy one DO get filtered. What bypasses it: records emitted through module-named loggers (bare structlog.get_logger() names the stdlib logger after the calling module, e.g. backend.adapters.live_ai_gemini), which are neither root nor noisy, so they reach root only by propagation (which skips root's filters). So the suppression covers some structlog output and misses most. Likely fix unchanged: attach the filter to the StreamHandler so it applies uniformly.

title: [bug] DisclaimerModal.test.tsx: 3 regex getByText assertions fail (pre-existing, all languages)
description:
Pre-existing test failure, NOT introduced by the Vite 6 / Vitest 3 upgrade -- verified identical 3-fail/83-pass on the dev baseline (Vite 5 / Vitest 1.6.1) and on Vite 6 / Vitest 3. frontend/src/schema-forms/components/DisclaimerModal.test.tsx lines 21, 28, 35 use regex getByText for the disclaimer BODY text in each language: - line 21 (English): /This tool helps you fill out your form/ - line 28 (Spanish): /Esta herramienta le ayuda a completar su formulario/ - line 35 (Chinese): /此工具帮助您填写表格/ All three fail with getElementError ('unable to find an element with text matching'). Root cause: the targeted phrase is a SUBSTRING of a longer paragraph rendered inside a

(DisclaimerModal.tsx ~L226-232 renders the disclaimer copy as p1/fullText-style blocks), but @testing-library getByText matches against a single text node's normalized full content -- a regex matching only part of a larger node does not match. The exact-string button assertions ('I Agree' / '我同意' / 'Important Notice' / '重要通知') PASS because buttons are their own nodes. Fix options (pick one): (a) use a custom text matcher / { exact: false } that searches within nodes, e.g. getByText((_, el) => el?.textContent?.includes('...')); (b) assert against container.textContent.includes(phrase); (c) wrap the targeted phrase in its own element in the component if it is semantically a heading/lead line. title: CLEAN-triggered deterministic bead close (pr_review_watcher --close-on-clean), replacing the manual post-CLEAN second call
description:
REPURPOSED (2026-06-02) after verifying the original premise was wrong. Original idea: a GitHub Action on pull_request closed+merged parses bead IDs from the PR body and closes them. That premise rested on "beads needs CI credentials to a separate Dolt remote" — FALSE. Beads syncs via `bd dolt push/pull` to its OWN remote (the git+https repo URL, [CLI only]); the tracked .beads/*.jsonl is a secondary mirror, not the transport. So no new CI secret was ever needed, AND the merge-trigger path is blocked anyway (the 'To Dev' ruleset requires a PR for any push to dev).

SHIPPED DESIGN (maintainer-steered): the deterministic post-CLEAN bead-close is driven by the LOCAL review watcher, not a GitHub Action. `pr_review_watcher.py --close-on-clean <bead-id>` closes the bead(s) ONLY on the CLEAN terminal state (never COMMENTS/ERROR/TIMEOUT/MERGED) by shelling out to `closeout_finish.py --close-only` (= bd_safe close -> bd dolt push). The watcher then wakes the orchestrator only for the merge ping — the old manual second `--close-only` call (one Opus turn) is removed. On a close failure the watcher exits CLOSE-FAILED (3) so the orchestrator triages instead of pinging a false "ready to merge".

KEY FACTS (why this works): (1) bead state syncs via bd dolt push independent of the PR/git — nothing to commit/push, no merge-race; the re-exported JSONL mirror is left dirty for the next manual bd sync (maintainer's call). (2) --close-only writes NO telemetry row, preserving the hrn.15 A/B discipline (no duplicate ledger row). (3) Idempotent: bd close of an already-closed bead is a no-op. (4) fresh-eyes race handled in SKILL: pass --close-on-clean on round 1 only once fresh-eyes is known empty; otherwise carry it on the re-watch (whose CLEAN is genuinely terminal).

SURFACES: scripts/pr_review_watcher.py (--close-on-clean flag + _close_beads_on_clean + EXIT_CLOSE_FAILED), .claude/skills/closeout/SKILL.md (Steps 6/7/8 + the two-call note), tests/test_pr_review_watcher.py (gating tests). Telemetry half (harness_ledger transcript parse) stays local regardless — unchanged.

title: Token-log section context is always null (set_session_context never called with a section id)
description: Fresh-eyes finding on PR #42 (bd polyglot-pdf-gfb.4), pre-existing (not introduced by the rename). LiveAIGemini.set_session_context(form_session_id, form_id, current_section_id=None) stores current_section_id into self._current_section_id, which is logged as the token-log payload key 'part_id' (token_file_logger). BUT no caller ever passes a non-None section id: form_filling_service.py:140 passes current_section_id=None ('# Will be updated on section switch'), and the other two callers (test_live_ai_gemini.py:350, scripts/spikes/measure_live_token_curve.py:143) omit it. switch_to_section routes through start_session, which calls set_session_context with None again. So _current_section_id is permanently None and every token_usage.jsonl event logs part_id: null -> the per-section cost breakdown the field was meant to provide is never populated. The '# Will be updated on section switch' comment promises an update that no code path performs. FIX: thread the current section id into set_session_context on session start AND on section switch (switch_to_section / start_session), so token events carry the real section. Coordinate with bd polyglot-pdf-zun (which renames the part_id key -> section_id on the log wire format) — ideally do both together so the key and its value land correctly. Acceptance: token_usage.jsonl events carry the active section id; a test asserts a non-null section in the logged event after a section switch.

description: Surfaced by fresh-eyes review of PR #23 (bd polyglot-pdf-8x5). On a mid-session restart of a multi-section form, the regenerated system instruction is stripped of section context, so Gemini may re-ask earlier-section fields or lose its position. Pre-existing (the line-380 comment acknowledges empty values for client-source-of-truth) and NOT addressed by the 8x5 callback fix; 8x5 only fixed the AttributeError. DO: thread the current section metadata into restart_gemini_session's build_form_context_message call (likely needs the service to retain last section metadata, or have the caller pass it), and add a multi-section restart test. Confidence: medium.
notes: STILL LIVE (verified 2026-06-04): restart_gemini_session (form_filling_service.py:379) still calls build_form_context_message(self._schema, {}) with NO section metadata, vs switch_to_section (line 537) which passes section_number/section_label/total_sections/previous_spoken_names. CONTEXT UPDATE: the related bead 7kp ('compression makes restarts moot') is now CLOSED as obsolete -- compression is a dead end on native-audio (bd l3a.1), so mid-session restarts are PERMANENT, not going away. That makes umv MORE relevant, not less: this is not a transient pre-compression wart, it's a standing correctness bug in a code path that stays. Scope unchanged: thread current section metadata into the restart path (service likely needs to retain last section metadata) + add a multi-section restart test.

title: Investigate Gemini Live code=1011 mid-turn failures on 2.5 native-audio preview (reported ~80% since 2026-05-27)

The other site (polyglot-forms-919f2) is abandoned (GCP blocked it). Re-scoped P1->P3 as a watch/reference item.
